Hurl a small plant that deals 100/150/200/250/300 (+100% magical power) magical damage over time to all Enemies in the area, exploding after 2s.
Untamed Growth deals 50% of its damage over its lifetime, and 50% upon exploding.

twinblast.reason: Attacks, Vaporize and Ventilate form the physical plan. Vortex Grenade supplies secondary magical control damage.

source_abilities.LMB: Ranged basic attack that fires two projectiles, each dealing 33 (+42.5% physical power) physical damage and applying on-hit effects at 55% effectiveness.
source_abilities.Q: TwinBlast charges and fires two superheated piercing projectiles in the target direction, dealing a total of 100/140/180/220/260 (+90% physical power)(+120% magical power) physical damage and applying on-hit effects to all Enemy Units hit at 170% effectiveness.
source_abilities.R:
Transform your guns into fully automatic machine guns, unleashing a barrage of 30 (+10% Total Attack Speed) bullets over 3s dealing 15/20/25 (+9% physical power)(+9% magical power) physical damage per bullet. 
Can Critically Strike at 75% effectiveness.

wraith.reason: Base Knock, Knock! and attacks are physical, while the mark adds magical damage. Mystic Marksman explicitly converts the shot; the enemy augment is unknown unless inspected.

source_abilities.E:
After a short delay, enter Camouflage and gain 25% movement speed and one enhanced Jump for 3s.
Takedowns will reset the cooldown of Surprise, Surprise!
Passive: Gain 10/14/18/22/26% Physical Penetration
source_abilities.Q:
Launch a piercing Nanite Grenade that deals 40/60/80/100/120 (+60% physical power)(+50% magical power) physical damage to all Units hit, Slowing them by 35% for 1.25s. Units hit are also Marked for 3.5s, Revealing them.
Knock, Knock! is enhanced against Marked Units, dealing an extra 5.5/6/6.5/7/7.5% (+1.5% magical power per 100 Magical Power) of their maximum health as bonus magical damage.
source_abilities.RMB:
Fire a long-range sniper shot that deals 20/35/50/65/80 (+110% physical power)(+70% magical power) physical damage to the first Enemy Unit hit. Damage is increased by 100% against Enemy Minions. Knock, Knock! benefits from lifesteal.
If Knock, Knock! Kills, or Damages a marked Unit, 35% of the Mana Cost is refunded and its Cooldown is decreased by 75%.

wukong.reason: The stance attacks and clone ultimate form physical pressure. Unverified item duplication on clones is excluded from this assessment.

source_abilities.E:
Spirit:
Wukong spins his staff around himself gaining 25% (+50% physical penetration) Damage Reduction for the duration. Afterwards he throws the staff forward dealing 60/80/100/120/140/160 (+70% physical power) damage and Stunning for 0.8s.
Body:
Wukong enlarges his staff and slams down to the ground dealing 60/100/140/180/220/260 (+135% physical power) damage and slowing by 40% for 0.75. This damage is increased by drop distance up to 1500 units. Minions receive 70% less damage.

Switch between Body and Spirit Stances

Leaving combat will reset the counter.

Wukong dashes forward dealing 60/85/110/135/160/185 (+100% physical power) damage and Slowing everything hit by 40% for 0.5s.

Wukong enlarges his staff sending it forward dealing 60/85/110/135/160/185 (+100% physical power) damage, Slowing for 30% for 0.75s and forcing away all enemies and Clones.

zinx.reason: The energized attack and damaging utility spells add magical pressure. Support restoration does not substitute for a dedicated damage plan.

guidance.historical_note: One-time review for patch 1.17, written on 23-24 September 2026 as a Gold+ (ranks 27-36) reference. Grades are dated editorial judgments, not win probabilities. Evidence limits: Pred.gg 1.17 Gold+ data covered about 1.5 days (fewer than 30 to about 770 games per hero and role, with intervals of roughly 4 to 18 points either way); Bronze+ figures contain the Gold+ games; the 14 September 1.16.4 review samples are large but from the previous patch; Statz is a lagging 1.16 comparison. Earlier council judgments and the 14 September review remain background, and observed rates, calculated kit fit and personal working pools stay separate.

maintenance_review.note: One-time review for Patch 1.17 of tiers, hero notes, counters, build adaptations, compositions and pools, over all 96 plans from the 1.17 build review. It does not start recurring AI reviews. Grades moved only with a kit or patch reason and evidence pointing the same way; most entries were retained with corrected text.
maintenance_review.rank_note: Gold+ remains the editorial reference. The Pred.gg Gold+ 1.17 sample was about 1.5 days old at review; Bronze+ contains the same games and is not independent. Statz still labels its dataset 1.16 and was used only for comparison.

meta_review.author: Claude (Opus 5.5) editorial strategy review, 2.34

entries.watch: Her offlane results improved in 1.17 without a kit change and remain below even. Tyrant of Thorns removes Royal Flourish's mesmerize, so the offlane damage plan is not the support peel plan.
entries.why: Iron Rose lets her trade up close, and Imperial Lash or Queen's Garden opens the damage window; Crown of Thorns helps allies convert contact.

entries.watch: Lower current role results temper the utility. Tyrant of Thorns removes Royal Flourish control, so the offlane damage plan is not the support peel plan.
entries.why: Imperial Lash and Iron Rose give a protected catch; Crown of Thorns helps allies convert contact.

entries.watch: B since the 3 Oct recheck: 1.17 cut his magical scaling and his jungle results fell below even. Keep the durable health route; interrupted Consume and repeated disengage still deny the plan.
entries.why: Crushing Maw sustains close trades and Web Lash creates access; Consume rewards a team that can keep targets nearby.

entries.watch: B since the 3 Oct recheck: in results the 1.17 magic-scaling cut outweighed the Crushing Maw health-scaling gain. Keep the durable health build rather than a burst plan; interrupted Consume and repeated disengage deny it.
entries.why: Crushing Maw sustains close trades and Web Lash creates access; Consume rewards a team that can keep targets nearby.

entries.watch: The midlane economy supports his damage engine; reposition before committing the beam channel. The early 1.17 sample has not shown a real decline, and 1.17 trimmed Lich in this plan's Vesh blessings.
entries.why: Dread Nova opens a ranged damage window and Particle Shredder can keep pressure on a caught target.

entries.watch: Support income limits his damage engine, and his previous-patch Gold+ support results were well below midlane. Pick him only when the team already has a durable entry.
entries.why: Dread Nova gives a repeatable ranged catch and Ether Crystal changes where the fight happens; Particle Shredder converts the opening when it is safe to channel.

entries.watch: Jungle is the priority on current role evidence. Do not transfer that grade to offlane or support, and keep an exit after the first control cycle.
entries.why: Glacial Charge, its Glacial Thorns root crystals and Hoarfrost give repeatable access, control and escape; Cryoseism can punish enemies gathering around an objective.

entries.watch: Jungle is the priority on current role evidence. Do not transfer that grade to offlane or support, and keep an exit after the first control cycle.
entries.why: Glacial Charge and Hoarfrost give repeatable access and escape; Cryoseism can punish enemies gathering around an objective.

entries.watch: Support results rose in 1.17 with no kit reason (the only change cut Shatter's on-hit scaling), so the grade stays B until a kit reason supports more. Do not transfer the jungle grade, and keep an exit after the first control cycle.
entries.why: Glacial Charge and Hoarfrost give repeatable access and escape; Cryoseism can punish enemies gathering around an objective.

entries.watch: Current results and committed entry make this a comfort pick. Avoid relying on disputed Berserk scaling or assuming faster attacks solve his access problems.
entries.why: Skull Crusher and Cursed Edge can set up a heavy-hit sequence, with Kingslayer converting a reachable catch.

entries.watch: Current results and committed entry make this a comfort pick. Avoid relying on disputed Berserk scaling or assuming faster attacks solve his access problems.
entries.why: Skull Crusher and Cursed Edge can set up a heavy-hit sequence, with Kingslayer converting a reachable catch.

entries.watch: Near-even results make this a dependable option rather than a statistical standout. Ursine Burst still needs allied follow-up and an exit plan.
entries.why: Detection Protocol helps locate a route into a fight; Chrono Swipe and Primeval Roar support sustained contact after entry.

entries.watch: A practiced option: the jungle sample since the fix is small and her roles did not all move together. Mark a safe Shadow Slip return point before committing Feast.
entries.why: Shadow Slip and Blade Siphon support short trades; the fixed Feast now gives a real targeted conversion after two abilities apply Haemorrhage.

entries.watch: The Feast fix restored her conversion and her 1.17 offlane results recovered above even. Mark a safe Shadow Slip return point and apply Haemorrhage before Feast.
entries.why: Shadow Slip and Blade Siphon support short trades; Feast converts a target after two ability hits apply Haemorrhage.

entries.watch: 1.17 restored Feast's intended damage, but midlane still asks a melee hero to trade into ranged lanes. Keep a safe Shadow Slip return and follow the jungler's catch rather than entering first.
entries.why: Shadow Slip and Blade Siphon support short trades; Feast converts a target after two ability hits apply Haemorrhage.

entries.watch: The combo breakpoint and sustained contact matter. A Ground effect now interrupts empowered Forward Crunch, so a lost escape can leave him stranded.
entries.why: Re-Crunch rewards correct ability sequencing and Cross Crunch attack weaving; Forward Crunch can preserve access for a second rotation.

entries.watch: The combo breakpoint and sustained contact matter. A Ground effect now interrupts empowered Forward Crunch, and a lost escape can leave him stranded.
entries.why: Re-Crunch rewards correct ability sequencing and Cross Crunch attack weaving; Forward Crunch can preserve access for a second rotation.

entries.watch: This grade values control despite below-even role results on both patches. Missed skill shots and poor fence timing reduce the benefit substantially.
entries.why: Control and projectile accuracy can still buy valuable attack time, but the dated Gold+ sample does not support default A priority. Choose for the needed fence and peel tools rather than treating kit fit as demonstrated pair success.

entries.watch: Keep a target in attack range. The airborne blast can displace enemies away from allies, and utility does not remove the need for a carry damage curve.
entries.why: Gag Grenade can deny a response while Rad Rounds supplies a damage window; Shrapnel Cannon adds armor shred and escape utility.

entries.watch: Heat and stance execution are essential. Her passive turns attack speed into physical power rather than firing speed, and she still needs a response to dive.
entries.why: Tachyon Lance/Axiom Strike and Zero Shift let Eden choose a trading pattern; in the Focal Lens plan, a Tachyon Lance hit shreds armor before the physical follow-through.

entries.watch: The dated jungle result was weak and early 1.17 results do not yet justify a higher grade. Ground now stops Reaping Dash's teleport; do not use the finishing ultimate as a substitute for an opening catch.
entries.why: Safeguard and Hamstring enable short ability-attack trades before Earth Shatter can finish a damaged target.

entries.watch: His offlane sample is small in both patches and favors specialists. Reaping Dash can no longer teleport while he is hit by a Ground effect, and the finishing ultimate is not an opening catch.
entries.why: Safeguard and Hamstring enable short ability-attack trades before Earth Shatter can finish a damaged target.

entries.watch: Midlane supplies the farming economy. 1.17 raised empowered mine damage and allied gate speed but made Security Gate cost more mana, so keep the gate for the exit or a diver rather than spending it freely.
entries.why: Sticky Mine pressures a position and Tesla Dome punishes enemies held in a choke; Security Gate provides an escape or peel route.

entries.watch: Midlane supplies the farming economy. Support is a smaller-sample damage-utility option when the team already has frontline and reliable initiation.
entries.why: Sticky Mine pressures a position and Tesla Dome punishes enemies held in a choke; Security Gate provides an escape or peel route.

entries.watch: 1.17 trimmed Void Breach, Black Hole, Event Horizon and his mana scaling, and Hotfix 1.17.1 removed a Black Hole bug that favored him, so he is an A conversion pick for a coordinated team. A Ground effect now stops Torn Space, and interrupts land once the Truesilver shield breaks.
entries.why: Cosmic Rift supports lane pressure while Torn Space preserves positioning; Black Hole offers a clear conversion for jungle or support control.

entries.watch: The strong offlane sample does not transfer to jungle, and 1.17 lowered his health and armor growth, so buy real defense early. Personal survival is not allied peel; the draft still needs a reliable catch.
entries.why: Make Way and Sacred Oath create sustained gank pressure; Stone Forged Soul can extend the time he occupies frontline space.

entries.watch: 1.17 lowered his base health and armor growth, and his 1.17 offlane results sit near even, so he is a strong lane-pressure option rather than the default. Buy real defense on time; personal survival is not allied peel, and the draft still needs a reliable catch.
entries.why: Make Way and Sacred Oath create sustained lane pressure; Stone Forged Soul can extend the time he occupies frontline space.

entries.watch: His 1.16.4 and 1.17 carry results sit below the leading carries; treat him as a practiced pick. Buy penetration for the magical damage he actually deals, and do not count the shield as a general escape.
entries.why: Assault Mode and Pulsefire provide a magical basic-attack threat; Energy Shield can preserve a firing window against an important spell.

entries.watch: Offlane is the preferred role. Long-trade strength does not guarantee access to a ranged target; Ground effects now interrupt Stampede, and anti-heal or disengage can stop the plan.
entries.why: Smash 'n Grab creates a reachable target and Double Pain rewards continued contact; Warlord's Challenge helps punish a committed melee fight.

entries.watch: Offlane is the preferred role. A Ground effect now interrupts Stampede, and long-trade strength does not guarantee access to a ranged target; anti-heal and disengage can stop the plan.
entries.why: Smash 'n Grab creates a reachable target and Double Pain rewards continued contact; Warlord's Challenge helps punish a committed melee fight.

entries.watch: Track the target throughout the ultimate. Movement during the barrage is not immunity, and a poorly aimed mine can spoil allied follow-up.
entries.why: R2000 Missile supports ranged pressure and Land Mine can protect an angle; Make It Rain follows a held target with an aimed barrage.

entries.watch: The strong offlane result needs composition context: pick ranged lane pressure when another slot supplies frontline. Rotations away from the prepared nest are less comfortable.
entries.why: Flame Turret and Oil Spill can control a lane approach and prepare objective space before the fight starts.

entries.watch: Supply frontline from another slot and set the nest before objectives; rotations away from it are less comfortable. Inferno's turret attack-speed text is a 1.17 description correction, not a new buff.
entries.why: Flame Turret and Oil Spill can control a lane approach and prepare objective space before the fight starts.

entries.watch: Current results favor a specialist pick. Bubble amplification timing, positioning and target access make nominal damage a poor guide to reliable output.
entries.why: Narcosis can create a catch for Hydroclasm and Brine; Genesis offers a further control and damage window.

entries.watch: The early 1.17 rise faded and her kit is unchanged. The fragile entry favors experienced players; vision, enemy peel and the escape route matter more than an attractive burst total.
entries.why: Shadow Walk can create an unseen angle and Crippling Dagger helps maintain it before Guillotine finishes a damaged target.

entries.watch: The large jungle sample is useful; weaker offlane evidence is a separate result. Anti-heal and disengage can deny sustain, especially beyond allied range.
entries.why: Ambush and Unleash support a direct jungle pressure pattern, with Cull converting a caught target and Invigorate extending contact.

entries.watch: The large jungle result does not transfer. His 1.17 offlane results have risen to about even, but nothing in 1.17 changed his kit and the interval still includes his weaker 1.16.4 result, so the grade stays until a kit reason agrees. Anti-heal and disengage can deny his sustain, especially beyond allied range.
entries.why: Ambush and Unleash give short trades once Lane Lurker builds Rage from minions; Cull converts a caught target and Invigorate extends contact.

entries.watch: 1.17 raised Mercy damage and Dusk now refunds mana on a kill, and her results since the review have risen with them. Purge is an exposed commitment that still needs control or peel, and the refund needs a kill.
entries.why: Mercy and repeated attacks build Vengeance before Dusk; Shadow Glide offers a way to preserve space or follow a confirmed catch.

entries.watch: His 1.16.4 samples and his 1.17 jungle results sit below even, so treat him as a practiced sword-placement option. The Grounded sword-pickup fix is a reliability change, not a reason to promote him.
entries.why: Judgement of the Heavens can tether a target for sword-centered follow-up; Light of the Heavens and Fury of the Heavens support repeated trades.

entries.watch: Both dated role samples were below even and early 1.17 results are too, so treat him as a practiced sword-placement option for controlled fights. The Grounded sword-pickup fix is a reliability change, not a reason to promote him.
entries.why: Judgement of the Heavens can tether a target for sword-centered follow-up; Light of the Heavens and Fury of the Heavens support repeated trades.

entries.watch: 1.17 widened the rifle projectile, but his 1.17 carry results stayed near even, below the S carries. The ability-oriented plan converts an allied catch, and bonus attack speed becomes haste, not firing speed.
entries.why: Saturation Charge and Orbital Sanction offer area pressure alongside ranged attacks; the Scorched Earth plan adds napalm zones where mines, Frag Order and the beam land.

entries.watch: Midlane has the stronger role evidence. A missed Seismic Assault line leaves little catch, and maximum-rank Innovation effects should guide skill investment.
entries.why: Seismic Assault gives a compact catch into Void Bomb; Neural Disruptor adds a finishing threat that depends on the target's mana state.

entries.watch: Midlane has the stronger role evidence. On a support budget Neural Disruptor carries less burst, so the grade rests on landing Seismic Assault for allies.
entries.why: Seismic Assault gives a compact catch into Void Bomb; Neural Disruptor adds a finishing threat that depends on the target's mana state.

entries.watch: His previous-patch Gold+ support sample was weak despite useful tools. Healing requires allies to stay in range, and spending Maco Fly! forward can leave him without an exit.
entries.why: Maco Gift! can sustain an ally around a chosen space, while Maco Strike! supplies control and Maco Fly! changes the supporting angle.

entries.watch: Still situational: Curse does not solve entering Mark range safely, and rank-one Mark is slower on 1.17. Pick her into a reachable target with allied control; the early 1.17 rise is a small sample.
entries.why: A shorter Hive cooldown and Mark set up close-range pressure and healing trades before Curse finishes the marked target.

entries.watch: Keep a defensive response after initiating. Eclipse connects distant pressure but should not be interpreted as relocating teammates.
entries.why: Abduct creates a catch while Contagion supplies allied sustain; Beguile offers another response as the fight develops.

entries.watch: 1.17 raised Shots Fired, Buckshot and Long Arm of the Law damage, but his 1.17 carry results fell below his previous patch, so he is a comfort or matchup pick. Save Buckshot and traps for the diver.
entries.why: Static Trap and Buckshot can buy firing space, while Long Arm of the Law converts a distant catch without abandoning the lane.

entries.watch: 1.17 trimmed her durability, passive amplification, Alacrity shield scaling and Reversal's damage reduction, and raised Reversal's cost; re-check the grade as 1.17 data grows. Choose her when the team supplies a way to begin fights.
entries.why: Consecrated Ground and Alacrity heal, shield and speed an attacking ally; Reversal Of Fortune can protect a committed teammate across the map.

entries.watch: Grouped sustain, March movement and a direct Thunk catch make him a priority for a team that actually stays in range. Hold the ultimate until interruption can be covered.
entries.why: Song Of My People and March! reward a team that moves together; Thunk supplies a catch before Crash Bang Boom! layers pressure.

entries.watch: A practiced pick: correct sequencing and a saved Erase Vector are needed, and true and magical damage use different penetration. Her early 1.17 rise faded toward even and has no kit change behind it.
entries.why: L.I.N.X and Final Thread offer a deliberate spell sequence, with Data Burst supporting the next empowered tool.

entries.watch: 1.17 lowered her health, Essence Catalyst healing and Hyperflux attack speed, so trades are less safe and amplification is slightly smaller. This stays a partner-dependent grade; a premature pull can undo a good commitment.
entries.why: Telekinetic Link and Hyperflux can amplify repeated attacks; Energy Lance and a timed pull can buy the linked ally space.

entries.watch: The plan's Rock & Awe rewards long boulder throws, so land the catch from range before committing Pounce. His 1.17 results sit just under even without a kit change; health does not guarantee uninterrupted target access.
entries.why: Boulder Throw creates an accessible catch and King of the Jungle supports the jungle route; Behemoth can extend frontline pressure.

entries.watch: The current sample does not support an automatic top-tier claim. Protect farming and the channel, and avoid collecting Essence through an exposed route.
entries.why: Soulfire and Stupor support wave pressure and catch conversion; Abyssal Rift gives a prepared team a sustained follow-up window.

entries.watch: Reckoning can remove a focus target from allied area damage. Coordinate isolation, and do not buy attack speed merely because it suits another carry.
entries.why: Hellfire Rounds and Obliterate reward a short damage window, making allied catches a natural way to convert his burst.

entries.watch: The grade depends on landing the hook. Keep an exit and preserve peel after a miss; his support catch is a separate job, and its grade does not transfer to jungle.
entries.why: Hook-dependent access and the dated weak Gold+ role result lower default jungle priority. His support catch remains a separate job; a landed hook can still enable excellent follow-up.

entries.watch: The grade depends on landing Riplash. Keep an exit and a second peel tool after a miss, and stay near allies who can convert the pull.
entries.why: Riplash into Shock Therapy or Skewer creates a dangerous pick when allies are in range to follow.

entries.watch: The grade depends on landing the hook. The dated offlane reference was weak and the early 1.17 sample does not justify a raise; keep an exit and preserve peel after a miss.
entries.why: Riplash into Shock Therapy or Skewer creates a dangerous pick when allies are in range to follow.

entries.watch: The larger positive offlane sample supports that role first. Jungle is a different result; manage energy and avoid relying on the disputed Ashen Vow base value.
entries.why: A committed, resource-sensitive entry plus the weak dated Gold+ jungle reference makes this a practiced specialist choice. The stronger offlane reference does not transfer to jungle.

entries.watch: Her early 1.17 offlane high has settled back near her 1.16.4 level, still above even over a large sample, which supports a serious alternative. Energy, exit execution and the unresolved Ashen Vow base field make this a more demanding default than Greystone.
entries.why: Minueta and First Intent support repeated ability pressure; Swan Song can convert a reachable target while the team follows.

entries.watch: 1.17 cut her on-hit and Heresy burn scaling and the Wind-Rider attack speed her plan uses, and early results fell. Enter after key enemy control is spent; a visage reset must be earned.
entries.why: Heaven's Fury and Heresy reward attack uptime after a catch; Crushing Descent gives Ascend a brief stun to open the entry.

entries.watch: The dated jungle result does not transfer to her small, weak offlane sample, and 1.17 trimmed the attack-uptime damage both roles use. Enter after key enemy control is spent rather than leading into every interrupt.
entries.why: Heaven's Fury and Heresy reward attack uptime after a catch; Ascend helps choose the entry and preserve a route through the fight.

entries.watch: Flagged: lowest B jungler with no 1.17 change; if a larger sample's interval excludes his 1.16.4 rate (47.7%) he drops to C. Protect the early soul-stacking route; Colossal Blow must not knock the target away from allied damage.
entries.why: Siphon and Reaper of Souls support a scaling frontline; Subjugate can hold a target for allies as durability develops.

entries.watch: Protect the early stacking route; Souls need ability kills. Colossal Blow must not eject the target from allied damage.
entries.why: Siphon and Reaper of Souls support a scaling frontline; Subjugate can hold a target for allies as durability develops.

entries.watch: Offlane is the more established option. Her 1.17 jungle results have risen above her 1.16.4 review rate, but nothing in 1.17 or Hotfix 1.17.1 changed her kit or her plan's items, so the grade stays until a kit reason agrees. She is a damage threat rather than the default damage sponge.
entries.why: Line Tempo and Circle Rhythm support repeated trades before All-Kill! converts accumulated pressure; Rushing Beat helps choose the exit.

entries.watch: Offlane is the more established option. She is a damage threat rather than the default damage sponge, and the jungle sample is relatively small.
entries.why: Line Tempo and Circle Rhythm support repeated trades before All-Kill! converts accumulated pressure; Rushing Beat helps choose the exit.

entries.watch: Her 1.16.4 and early 1.17 carry results sit below the leading options. Flight is not guaranteed safety; choose a peel partner, and remember the Satariel plan loses its takedown stacks on death.
entries.why: Air Assault can change the firing angle while Hypercharge provides a committed damage window.

entries.watch: This priority assumes someone buys attack time. There is no dash to rescue an exposed path, and the initial control will not last for the entire barrage.
entries.why: Relentless and Heightened Senses reward safe repeated attacks; Inner Fire turns an allied control window into a sustained barrage.

entries.watch: Support is his established role; offlane Steel brings utility more than lane pressure. On 1.17 Heavy Metal attacks do not remove spell shields.
entries.why: Cybernetic Shell and Shield Bash let him hold the wave, then Shield Slam and Force Shield make him a team-catch and projectile-protection pick rather than a solo-lane threat.

entries.watch: Heavy Metal basic attacks no longer break spell shields on 1.17, so keep a separate answer for one before engaging. Catch value depends on allied damage close enough to convert Shield Slam.
entries.why: Shield Bash and Shield Slam provide clear catch conversion, while Force Shield can protect an approach or the backline.

entries.watch: Jungle rests on a much smaller sample than support. His 1.17 jungle results sit below even and below his 1.16.4 review rate, though not clearly, and the only 1.17 change to his plan is the narrow Heavy Metal spell-shield interaction, so A stays for now; it drops to B if a larger sample's interval excludes 52.6%. Heavy Metal attacks no longer break spell shields, so bring a real answer before engaging.
entries.why: Shield Bash and Shield Slam provide clear catch conversion, while Force Shield can protect an approach or the backline.

entries.watch: Dated results in both roles were weak and 1.17 made no Terra changes. The small jungle sample is not a default recommendation; use her as a practiced control answer.
entries.why: Ruthless Assault and Highland Hurl can pressure a held target; Unstoppable Force helps a committed frontline sequence.

entries.watch: Her offlane results stayed weak into 1.17. Keep her as a practiced answer to a specific draft, not a default.
entries.why: Ruthless Assault and Highland Hurl can pressure a held target; Unstoppable Force helps a committed frontline sequence.

entries.watch: Midlane has the larger established sample. Support is a smaller-sample option needing frontline elsewhere, and the delayed ultimate still needs setup or a constrained path.
entries.why: Harvest Nettles supports repeated lane pressure; Fly Trap and Bramble Patch turn constrained movement into a clear follow-up opportunity.

entries.watch: Midlane has the larger established sample. Support is a smaller-sample option needing frontline elsewhere, and the delayed ultimate still needs setup or a constrained path.
entries.why: Harvest Nettles supports repeated lane pressure; Fly Trap and Bramble Patch turn constrained movement into a clear follow-up opportunity.

entries.watch: 1.17's larger basic-attack hitbox helps consistency, not listed damage, and his results remain below the carry priorities. Do not spend the dash forward while a diver is missing or channel Ventilate into an available interrupt.
entries.why: Vaporize and Vortex Grenade support ability-attack weaving; Rocket Dash lets him preserve a firing position or follow a confirmed catch.

entries.watch: Carry has the better role result. The midlane plan stays physical with Sniper's Bounty, so missed shots cost both damage and gold; 1.17 trimmed Demonic Bargain and Satariel, which this plan uses.
entries.why: Peekaboo! marks a target for repeated Knock, Knock! shots with attacks between casts; Back It Up! returns a target to where the team can follow.

entries.watch: No dash: crowd control on Valmont, broken line of sight or distance breaks the bind, and Exsanguinate costs more mana each second it stays on, so toggle it off between fights. His Gold+ midlane results sit near even, so treat him as a practiced pick.
entries.why: Arterial Grip grounds and slows a bound target so Rupture and Bloodbound can land, and Exsanguinate's bats return health, far more when they hit heroes. The grounding bind also stops dashes such as Torn Space.

entries.watch: Mystic Marksman makes Knock, Knock! magical while his attacks and the grenade's hit stay physical, so penetration must fit both. Missed shots sharply reduce this plan's value.
entries.why: Peekaboo! marks a target so Knock, Knock! fires again sooner, with ranged attacks between casts; Back It Up! returns a target to where the team can follow.

entries.watch: 1.17 traded some health and armor for attack speed and cleave, so do not treat his damage plan as sole frontline coverage. The jungle sample is smaller than established staples; do not assume clones copy item on-hit effects.
entries.why: Cyclebreaker/High Impact and stance mobility support repeated pressure; 84000 Hairs can create an additional threat after a favorable entry.

entries.watch: A Ground effect now interrupts Lash Kick, so keep another exit. Reflection timing and target access decide whether her projectile tools matter.
entries.why: Windburn's extended attacks reward reliable attack time after a mid or support catch, and Backlash and Quelling Gale protect that window from projectiles. She still needs a separate initiator.

entries.watch: The offlane sample is small in both patches. A Ground effect now interrupts Lash Kick; reflection timing and target access decide whether her projectile tools matter.
entries.why: Windburn and repeated attacks create sustained pressure, while Backlash and Quelling Gale offer tools against projectile-based threats.

entries.watch: C since the 3 Oct recheck: results fell below even after 1.17 made Ground effects interrupt Soulstorm. Resets need a Soul Rip target; preserve a marked route that can also serve as an exit.
entries.why: Severance and Soulstorm can convert marked targets into an extended sequence, with Hallowed Strikes rewarding attacks between casts.

entries.watch: The stronger jungle result and easy-to-coordinate containment support this priority. Offlane is weaker, and Coliseum still needs an ally close enough to exploit it.
entries.why: Barricade and Coliseum offer a clear catch for midlane or support follow-up; Evade helps him remain active through the next exchange.

entries.watch: Jungle is his priority role; offlane is weaker in both the dated and the early 1.17 samples. Coliseum still needs an ally close enough to exploit it.
entries.why: Barricade and Coliseum offer a clear catch for midlane or support follow-up; Evade helps him remain active through the next exchange.

entries.watch: The offlane sample is modest on 1.16.4 and very small on 1.17. 1.17 raised both attack speed and base attack time, so it is not a plain attack-speed buff, and the Infuse change mainly helps the support plan.
entries.why: Refibrillator attacks with Bad Medicine and Ricochet give a ranged attack-and-spell lane with a stun, and Neural Regenesis can save a planned fight; another slot must supply frontline.

entries.watch: 1.17 raised Infuse's missing-health healing and shortened early Neural Regenesis cooldowns, but her 1.17 support results sit just under even, below the leading enchanters. Do not treat the offlane damage plan as the support plan.
entries.why: Infuse heals a damaged ally, Ricochet can create a catch, and Neural Regenesis protects a planned fight.

meta_review.method: Authored judgments from 1.17 kits, official 1.17 changes, current plans and role economy, weighed against Pred.gg Gold+ role results. A grade moved only with a kit or patch reason and evidence pointing the same way. The 1.17 Gold+ sample was about 1.5 days old (roughly 1,000 games per role; Bronze+ contains the same games), so where a role had fewer than 100 current Gold+ games the listed sample is the 1.16.4 review sample. Grades are not calculated win probabilities, source-provided tiers, or proven optimal picks. A 3 percentage-point change from the listed sample with at least 500 current games flags the grade for review; that trigger is not a significance test. Refreshing data does not rewrite this review. A grade recheck on 27 September 2026 re-examined the 21 grades the review flagged or the engine withheld, and gave Baron Valmont midlane his first grade, against about five days of the whole 1.17 line (1.17 plus Hotfix 1.17.1). It kept the review's standard (a kit or patch reason with evidence pointing the same way; a high rate alone never raises a grade), and added one rule: a grade may drop one step without a kit reason when the whole-line 95% interval excludes the previous-patch review rate with at least 500 games and the games since the review point the same way. Rechecked entries show their own date and cite the rechecked sample.
meta_review.scope: General ranked planning for Patch 1.17 with composition-specific conditions; Gold+ evidence. One-time review; no claim of a professional-play or all-rank consensus.

tier_definitions.A: Strong alternative with a clear role or enabling condition.
tier_definitions.B: Situational or practiced pick; check what the team needs.
tier_definitions.C: Lower default priority in this review; favor comfort or a favorable matchup.
tier_definitions.S: Priority starting point for its stated job; still depends on draft and execution.

guidance.note: Written guidance is editorial judgment, not a statistical ranking. A data refresh does not author new strategic advice.
notes: Jungle: Zarus (containment for a mid or support to convert) and Aurora (layered magical control) are the S starting points on 1.17. Serath moved to A: 1.17 trimmed her on-hit and Heresy burn scaling and the Wind-Rider attack speed her plan uses, so she is the second-wave diver rather than the first pick. Khaimera (A) has the steadiest large early 1.17 jungle sample for sustained pressure. Steel is the direct tank catch, with a very small early jungle sample and Heavy Metal attacks that no longer break spell shields. Rampage stays A as a durable long-range boulder catch; most of his early 1.17 dip did not persist (27 Sep recheck).

Mid: Lt. Belica (compact catch) and The Fey (prepared area control) stay S. Gideon moved to A on the 27 Sep recheck: 1.17 trimmed his damage, Hotfix 1.17.1 removed a Black Hole bug that favored him, and his results fell below his previous patch. A Ground effect such as Valmont's bind now stops Torn Space, so protect his entry and channel. Argus, Gadget and Howitzer are A alternatives; Morigesh rose to B on her Hive and Curse buffs. Valmont's first grade is B (27 Sep recheck): a grounding bind with sustain and no dash, near even over 1,354 Gold+ midlane games.

Carry: Drongo, Sparrow and Eden stay S. Drongo supplies silence and physical shred, Sparrow needs protected attack time, and Eden rewards practiced heat and stance management. Legion moved to A on the 27 Sep recheck: his 1.17 results stayed near even, below the other S carries and his previous patch; his Scorched Earth plan still adds area pressure. Revenant and Kira are the A alternatives; Kira rose to A once her results since the review followed her Mercy and Dusk buffs. Murdock returned to C: his 1.17 buffs did not lift his results. GRIM.exe's early drop has recovered toward his previous level.

Support: choose Steel for a direct opening, Mourn for catch plus sustain, Muriel for amplification and protection when initiation already exists, or Narbash for a grouped fight. Muriel keeps S after broad 1.17 trims, including a weaker and costlier Reversal, so position her carefully. Phase stays A after health and Hyperflux trims. Riktor remains a B hook-execution option; his 1.17 results settled near his previous patch. Dekker's B is flagged: his 1.17 support results are the lowest of the supports (27 Sep recheck).

Offlane: Greystone moved to A on the 27 Sep recheck: 1.17 lowered his base health and armor growth and his results fell to near even, so he is a strong lane-pressure option rather than the default. Stone Forged Soul is a 2.5s stasis heal, not an extra life. Grux now leads the working pool: he punishes reachable melee fights, though a Ground effect interrupts Stampede. Shinbi supplies magical skirmishing. Akeron, B since the 3 Oct recheck, still supplies sustain and frontline on a health build. Scarlett and Iggy & Scorch are strong alternatives, Iggy only when another role supplies frontline. Countess's offlane results recovered after the Feast fix. Terra and Serath offlane stay C and do not inherit another role's grade.

Pred.gg 1.17 matchup rows cover about 1.5 days and pool all roles, and the counter, anti-counter and lane-counter views are one table, not separate evidence. They describe observed games with the named hero present, not proof of a lane or ability interaction. Use the reviewed counterplay to decide which response you can execute.

Community builds are alternative hypotheses. The 2.32 build review compared their item sequences with 1.17 item effects and your role plan; popularity or a high conditional build rate cannot establish that a purchase caused the wins.

Patch 1.17 strategy review (23-24 September 2026) is a one-time pass, not a recurring schedule. Tier grades, hero notes, counter picks, build adaptations, compositions and pools were re-checked against exact 1.17 ability text, the official 1.17 notes and the 2.32 plans. Grades moved only where a kit or patch reason and the evidence pointed the same way: Serath jungle S to A, Countess jungle C to B, Morigesh midlane C to B and Murdock carry C to B. A grade recheck on 27 September 2026, after Hotfix 1.17.1 and about five days of 1.17 data, re-examined 21 flagged or withheld grades and graded Valmont: Kira carry B to A; Legion carry, Gideon midlane and Greystone offlane S to A; Murdock carry back to C. The other 16 were retained with rebased reference samples. Valmont midlane received his first grade, B.
