- [Bugfix] Zinx no longer extends her Stack Duration when damaging Heroes while she has Max Triage Protocol Stacks, which would prevent it from going on cooldown at the correct time.
- [QoL] Upon gaining maximum Triage Protocol Stacks, Zinx removes any currently active Basic Attack Penalty.

Refibrillator [Basic Attack]:
- Damage Over Time per Tick increased from 3-13.2 (+0.6 per level) to 4-14.2 (+0.6 per level).

Ricochet [Primary]:
- Damage decreased from 75/100/125/150/175 to 65/90/115/140/165.
- Initial Projectile no longer has bonus Homing towards targets.
- Cast Notify decreased from 5.5 to 5.2.
- Projectile Range increased from 1500 to 1575.
- Projectile Speed increased from 3000 to 3250.

Bad Medicine [Secondary]:
- Damage Radius increased from 260u to 280u.
- Explosion Radius increased from 260u to 280u.
- Projectile Speed increased from 3000 to 3400.
- Projectile Gravity increased from 1.25x to 1.4x.
- Gravity now increases to 1.8x after travelling 1000u.

Neural Regenesis [Ultimate]:
- Resurrection Healing changed from 35%/45%/55% to 400/750/1100 (+200% Magical Power).
- Resurrection Healing now benefits from Heal & Shield Power.
- Resurrection Mana Restore changed from 35%/45%/55% to 250/400/550 (100% Magical Power).

Soulbearer
- Anima Shield changed from (+25% Max Mana) to 100 (+40% Magical Power)(+8% Max Mana).

Ruthless Broadsword
- Corrode Physical Armor Shred decreased from 4.5% to 4%.

Void Crystal
- Lesser Fiend now has a 1s Cooldown.
- Lesser Fiend Stack Duration increased from 3 to 4.5s.

Nuclear Rounds:
- Attack Speed increased from 40% to 45%.
- Ability Haste increased from 15 to 20.

Onixian Quiver:
- Attack Speed increased from 40% to 45%.

Sky Splitter:
- Rend Ranged Damage increased from 3.5% to 4%.
- Rend Melee Damage increased from 5.5% to 6%.

Solaris:
- Solarblade Damage decreased from 50 to 45.

Spectra:
 -Reworked description be more clear.
- Radiant Strikes On-Hit Damage decreased from 25 to 20.
- Radiant Strikes now always applies Prism stacks On-Hit, even if the Item’s Effect is on cooldown.
- Prism stacks can now be applied to Monsters.
- Prisma can now trigger against Monsters.
- [Bugfix] Stacks now correctly last 2.5s, not 2s.

Viper:
 - Corrode Physical Armor Shred decreased from 4.5% to 4%.

Basilisk:
- Corrode Physical Armor Shred decreased from 4.5% to 4%.
- Eminence Movement Speed increased from 5% to 8%.

Amulet Of Chaos:
- Magical Penetration decreased from 12 to 10.

Azure Core:
- Spirit Shield changed from 20% Max Mana to 80 (+15% Max Mana).

Lifecore:
- Healing Wisp Magical Power Scaling decreased from 50% to 40%.

Megacosm:
- Cost decreased from 3100 to 3000.
- 250 Health added.
- 300 Mana removed.
- Recipe: Chaotic Core + Chronomatic Wand + 900g.

Oathkeeper:
- Celestial Spellblade Damage decreased from 65 to 60.

Worldbreaker:
- Fiend Cooldown increased from 0.5s to 1s.

Fire Blossom:
- Physical Armor increased from 45 to 50.
- Heatwave Damage decreased from 18 to 15.
- Heatwave Bonus Health Scaling decreased from 1% to 0.8%.

Inquisition:
- Psywave Cooldown increased from 1s to 1.5s.
If you’re reading this, congratulations, you’ve reached the end!
Putting this update together has been a tremendous amount of work, and the amount of reading we’ve just put in front of you is pretty symbolic of that.

As a reminder, the V1.12 balance patch is arriving earlier than usual on Tuesday, March 10th, so we’ll see you again very soon. Don’t hesitate to let us know what you think of all the changes when V1.12 launches next Tuesday, February 24th.
Game Design and Community @ Omeda Studios
articles.title: V1.12 Patch Notes

blocks: Everything you need to know about V1.12.4!
This time, we’re a little early - the schedule is a bit different as we want to ensure our PCC tournament is played on the most balanced build possible.
This is the first of two planned balance patches for V1.12. The first arrives on Tuesday, March 10th, with the second expected on March 24th.

This balance patch has big shoes to fill. V1.12 was one of the largest balance updates we’ve ever released - after all, every single Hero was affected. We’re very grateful for your feedback, and we hope you’ll find changes here that address your concerns.
Read on to find out more!

This update brings Daybreak V2 - a newer, improved version of our new map. It’s not final (V3 is already planned), but V2 should already address some of the biggest pain points we’ve seen, both from you and from our own testing, with Daybreak V1.
You can read more about the differences between Daybreak V1 and V2 in the blog here.
These bundles are available for a limited time only. All proceeds from bundle sales go toward funding our esports initiatives.
Speaking of esports, our Spring Open Qualifier is streaming next weekend - stay tuned!
A reminder that we’re currently running a Friend Reward competition! Encourage your friends to try Predecessor for a chance to win an iPhone 17 Pro or a million Platinum to spend in game!
You can find out more about the contest here.
World Shift: Frostfall will be temporarily disabled starting with the launch of this update on March 10th, for a period of at least two weeks, until March 24th.
Please keep in mind that these jungle camp changes apply to the Daybreak map only. Jungle camps on the Sanctuary map in Standard or Ranked will remain as they are right now.

White Camp:
- S - 500 (-50 per level)
- M - 730 (-70 per level)
- L - 1200 (-100 per level until level 5)

Brown Camp:
- S - 580 (-40 per level)
- M -1300 (-100 per level)

Black Camp:
- M - Daybreak: 920 (-80 per level)
- L - 1430 (-120 per level)

Grey Camp
- S - 620 (-30 per level)
- L- 1150 (-100 per level)
Akeron is receiving some minor increases to his level 1 damage, better normalizing his damage potential and clear speed for the Jungle and Offlane roles to be more in line with his competitors.

General:
- Physical Power increased from 60 to 62.

Crushing Maw [Alternate]:
- Damage increased from 60/80/100/120/140 to 65/85/105/125/145.

Aurora’s damage output, considering her disruptive and more tank-skewed profile, is currently too high. We’re reducing the general damage output she possesses to ensure there is a greater distinction between her damage potential when opting into tank or damage orientated builds, and that her general burst output is at more reasonable levels.

Hoarfrost [Secondary]:
- Magical Power Scaling decreased from 60% to 55%.

Boreal Sweep [Alternate]:
- Explosion damage decreased from 80/115/150/185/220 to 80/110/140/170/200.

Cryoseism [Ultimate]:
- Secondary Damage decreased from 80/120/160 to 70/105/140.
- Secondary Damage Magical Power Scaling decreased from 28% to 25%.

Argus currently possesses incredible pressure in the early lane thanks to the ease at which he can shove the wave and take a follow up fight. Likewise, his general presence throughout a match with the combination of stuns and consistent damage results in him being an overly effective combatant at all stages of a match. To help take the edge off, we’re shifting around his Mana economy and waveclearing capabilities at level 1, meaning he will run dry on Mana faster if he uses Particle Shredder too recklessly in the lane. Likewise, we are also reducing his general damage and Dread Nova uptime in the later stages of a match, reducing his overall effectiveness slightly in fights.

Mana Catalyst [Augment]:
- Non-Hero Mana restore decreased from 2% to 1.5%.

General:
- Mana decreased from 480 to 450.
- Mana Regen increased from 1.2 to 1.5.

Dread Nova [Primary]:
- Cooldown increased from 13/12/11/10/9 to 14/13/12/11/10.

Particle Shredder [Alternate]:
- Magical Power Scaling decreased from 20% to 18%.

Countess currently runs herself out of Mana a little too fast, even in the Jungle where her Mana Economy is more forgiving. We’re reducing the Mana Cost of Shadow Slip to ensure she is not overly punished for using it to navigate the map efficiently, while also increasing its damage to give more value to her Shadow Echo Augment especially, better allowing it to compete with the alternatives as it now supplements her burst further across a match.

Shadow Slip [Primary]:
- Magical Power Scaling increased from 30% to 40%.
- Cost decreased from 90 to 80.

Drongo currently struggles to compete among the Carry roster, with his general damage and laning strength faltering by comparison. Some small general power increases are needed are being granted to bring him up to speed, with Old Rusty now being more desirable to invest levels into in harder lane matchups, and both his Wastelander and Rad Rounds becoming more threatening when stacked up, regardless of whether he’s pumping rounds into a tank or a squishy.

Wastelander [Passive]:
- Max Health Damage increased from 2% to 2.25%.

Rad Rounds [Secondary]:
- Total Physical Power Scaling increased from 20% to 22%.

Old Rusty [Alternate]:
- Damage increased from 45/60/75/90/105 to 45/65/85/105/125.

Feng Mao is currently lagging behind other Junglers, unable to keep pace despite not having the greatest of utility tools to compete with other bruisers and tanks. A small but meaningful increase to Hamstring’s damage is needed to enhance his general clear speeds and early/mid-game gank threat (which of course helps Offlane Feng too!)

Hamstring [Secondary]:
- Damage increased from 36/48/64/76/88 to 42/56/70/84/98.
- Isolation Damage changed from 27/36/48/57/66 to 25/36/47/58/69.

Thanks to the shift towards Mana Scaling, Gideon finds himself thriving in the new balance environment, possessing both incredible laning strength, and immense lategame scaling. We’re targeting a few things in order to bring his general strength closer to the baseline that v1.12 was designed to set, with reductions to his Mana Conversion, damage, and Void Beach uptime all occurring, as they all currently contribute to his general strength and versatility.

Cosmic Power [Passive]:
- Mana from Magical Power conversion changed from 1% every 10 to 1% every 15.
- [Bugfix] Bonus Mana amount corrected to be more accurate in the in-game description.

Cosmic Rift [Primary]:
- Magical Power Scaling decreased from 65% to 60%.

Void Breach [Alternate]:
- Cooldown increased from 9/8.5/8/7.5/7 to 10/9.5/9/8.5/8.

Grim is currently blasting through his foes too quickly. Some general reduction to his overall DPS are needed to ensure he’s not spiking too hard once a few items are acquired. Likewise, Grim’s Ultimate is capable of dealing excessive damage in specific builds, and while we don’t want to entirely reduce the build variety here, some reductions to G.T.F.O’s damage is needed to ensure it’s a little more reasonable.

Assault Mode [Secondary]:
- Bonus Attack Speed per Stack decreased from 6%/9%/12%/15%/18% to 6%/8.5%/11%/13.5%/16%.
- Assault Mode Total Physical Power Scaling decreased from 15% to 12.5%
- Assault Mode Magical Power Scaling decreased from 10% to 9%.

G.T.F.O [Ultimate]:
- Damage decreased from 300/575/850 to 300/520/740.
- Bonus Physical Power Scaling decreased from 140% to 135%.
- Magical Power Scaling decreased from 120% to 110%.

One of the goals of Grux’s changes in v1.12 was to limit his potential as an excessive lane bully in exchange for more general utility and mobility across a match . Currently, he continues to stat-check his lane opponents a little too hard in various Offlane matchups, going against our goal. As a result we’re nudging down his early lane durability, meaning he must consider his early engagement windows with a little more care if he wishes to avoid death, and thereby opening up the range of matchups that can deal with him further.

General:
- Health decreased from 670 to 660.
- Physical Armor decreased from 35 to 32.

Double Pain [Alternate]:
- Missing Health Healing decreased from 6%/8%/10%/12%/14% to 5%/7%/9%/11%/13%.

For Howitzer, we have received general feedback that his R2000 feels like it takes a little too long to charge and leaves him a sitting duck while in that state. While we want Howitzer to commit to charging his missile to achieve a greater payoff as one of his unique loops, we acknowledge that the downsides are currently outweighing the payoffs, and have made some general adjustments to its damage potential, charge cadence and hover speed. Additionally, some general cooldown adjustments are occurring, allowing Howi’ to better compete with the other more powerful Mages across a match.

R2000 Missile [Primary]:
Damage increased from 75/115/155/195/235 to 85/125/165/205/245.
Hover Speed increased from 50% to 60%.
Max Charge Time decreased from 0.9s to 0.8s.
Max Hover Time decreased from 1.4s to 1.3s.

Land Mine [Secondary]:
Cooldown decreased from 20/18/16/14/12 to 18/16.5/15/13.5/12.

Slow Grenades [Secondary]:
Cooldown decreased from 18/17.5/17/16.5/16 to 16/15.5/15/14.5/14.

Kallari has emerged as one of the higher beneficiaries of the v1.12 changes, with her damage potential and general threat leading to moments of excessive damage, even if she sometimes misses her daggers. Some general damage reductions are occurring across the board, better ensuring Kallari must both choose and execute on her engagements with precision if she wishes to take down her target.

Deadly Finesse [Augment]:
- Crippling Dagger Cooldown Refund decreased from 2s to 1.5s.

Execution Mandate [Augment]:
- Cooldown Refund on Takedown decreased from 45% to 40%.

General:
- Physical Power decreased from 63 to 60.

Plasteel Swords [Basic Attack]:
- Bonus Physical Power Scaling decreased from 90% to 85%.

Crippling Dagger [Alternate]:
- Damage decreased from 70/100/130/160/190 to 65/95/125/155/185.

Guillotine [Ultimate]:
- Total Physical Power Scaling decreased from 70%/85%/100% to 65%/75%/85%.

Khaimera’s changes to a Rage machine have returned him to his former glory as the demon of the Jungle. This is largely thanks to the amount of regeneration and durability he has access to, especially with his Cooldown Progression mechanic allowing him repeat access to Invigorate which can lead to moments of borderline immortality. To account for his faster cooldown cadence, adjustments are needed to heavily tone down his general healing and cooldown output, better bringing him in line.

Invigorate [Secondary]:
- Healing Health Regen Multiplier decreased from 1.75x to 1.5x.
- Cooldown increased from 22/20.5/19/17.5/16 to 25/24/23/22/21.

Kira is receiving a small set of changes, primarily aimed at reducing the speed at which she melts through opponents with her Ultimate. In return for some of this lost damage, we’re granting back some damage to Mercy, better enabling her to prioritise maxing Dusk or Mercy first, based on her matchups and build.

Purge [Ultimate]:
- Total Physical Power Scaling decreased from 525% to 480%

The shift from Health Cost to Mana Cost for Maco’s heal helped unburden his playstyle with additional complexity, but the transition was not correctly tuned in order to Mana-gate his excessive heal spam appropriately. Likewise, now that Maco can heal himself he has become even more of a speed demon, able to zoom around the map as he desires. The mix of these factors means he requires some heavy adjustments to his Mana economy, better ensuring he cannot freely spam Maco Gift as he desires. Likewise, now that he moves at mach 10 speed, general reductions to his speed buffs are required to ensure his general mobility returns to a fast, but fair level.

General:
Mana increased from 320 to 340.
Mana Growth decreased from 50 to 45.
Mana Regen decreased from 2 to 1.6.
Mana Regen Growth increased from 0.12 to 0.15.

Mach Speed! [Passive]:
Movement Speed decreased from 15%-27.75% (+0.75% per Level) to 10%-20.2% (+0.6% per Level).
Falloff Delay decreased from 2.5s to 1.5s.

Maco Gift! [Primary]:
Damage decreased from 75/110/145/180/215 to 75/105/135/165/195.
Movement Speed Duration decreased from 3s to 2.5s.
Mana Cost increased from 50/55/60/65/70 to 50/60/70/80/90.

Maco Fly! [Secondary]:
Cooldown increased from 15/14/13/12/11 to 15/14.25/13.5/12.75/12.

Morigesh’s general strength has been on the excessive side with the release of v1.12, with her ability to heal through and cut down opponents being far too great. While we’re happy with the general shape of her power-curve and the general reception of changes to her abilities, the power is clearly far too high and in need of heavy adjustments. As a result, we’re shifting down a lot of Morigesh’s damage output, durability, and general healing capabilities, better ensuring that she remains weaker in the early lane and less of a crazy scaling threat late-game.

Ritual Of Death [Augment]:
- Healing decreased from 80%/100%/120% to 80%/90%/100%.

General:
- Physical Power decreased from 53 to 52.
- Physical Armor decreased from 22 to 20.
- Attack Speed increased from 125 to 130.
- Basic Attack Time increased from 1.45 to 1.5.

Pestilence [Passive]:
- Max Health Damage decreased from 0.25% to 0.18%.
- Magical Power Scaling decreased from 0.06% to 0.05%.

Hive [Primary]:
- Magical Power Scaling decreased from 70% to 65%.

Swarm [Secondary]:
- Hero Healing decreased from 45% to 40%.
- Damage Reduction decreased from 15% to 12%.
- Duration decreased from 4s to 3.5s.

Mark [Alternate]:
- Magical Power Scaling decreased from 50% to 45%.
- Healing Magical Power Scaling decreased from 28% to 25%.
- Additional Healing per Pestilence Stack decreased from 25% to 15%.
- Mana Refund on Kill decreased from 100% to 65%.
- Cooldown increased from 6/5.5/5/4.5/4 to 7/6.25/5.5/4.75/4.

Now that Mourn has access to Contagion on Eclipse by default, his general ability to collapse on targets with his new Nightstalker Augment, and the ability to burn through the enemies with Magical Builds is slightly too oppressive and in need of tuning down.

Nightstalker [Augment]:
- Movement Speed decreased from 80%/160%/300% to 70%/150%/280%.

Contagion [Primary]:
- Damage Magical Power Scaling decreased from 10% to 8%.

If you’ve ever been Buckshot in the head by a Murdock, you’ll know that thing hurts. Pair that with a late-game Shot’s Fired proc, and Murdock’s general damage output and burst is simply too high. This leads to excessive scenarios that warp the Time To Kill for various engagements. While we don’t want to negate their strength too heavily, drops in power for both are needed to ensure combat engagements with Murdock feel more appropriate.

Shots Fired [Passive]:
- Total Physical Power Scaling decreased from 40%/55%/70%/85% to 40%/52%/64%/76%.

Buckshot [Alternate]:
- Damage decreased from 100/128/156/184/212 to 80/108/136/164/192.
- Total Physical Power Scaling decreased from 120%/140%/160%/180%/200% to 100%/120%/140%/160%/180%.

Muriel’s rework has seen her emerge as one of the top Supports thanks to all the new agency she possesses. While this is great for Muriel, her general strength alongside her new tools lead to her feeling overly oppressive to deal with, especially when she is paired with Healers or Divers as her enchantments push them too far over the power-line in many cases. Due to this, she is in need of some adjustments across the board, better toning down areas of excess strength.

General:
- Mana Regen decreased from 2.2 to 2.
- Mana Regen Growth increased from 0.1 to 0.12.

Sentinel [Primary]:
- Ally Heal & Shield Power decreased from 12%-24.75% (+0.75% per Level) to 12%-20.5% (+0.5% per Level).

Consecrated Ground [Primary]:
- Damage decreased from 120/150/180/210/240 to 100/130/160/190/220.

Serenity [Alternate]:
- Stun and Slow Duration decreased from 1.05/1.1/1.15/1.2/1.25 to 1/1.05/1.1/1.15/1.2.
- Cooldown increased from 11/10.25/9.5/8.75/8 to 12/11.25/10.5/9.75/9.

Reversal Of Fortune [Ultimate]:
- Shield decreased from 400/650/900 to 280/480/680.
- Damage Reduction decreased from 50% to 40%.

While strong in his own right, Narbash can feel a little unsatisfying to play as currently due to his general healing output being on the low end compared to before, making him feel overshined by other enchanters. Likewise, the cooldown of his Toggle can feel overly long, reducing the finesse at which he flick through songs and march casts, and thereby making him feel overly-unresponsive to play. We’ve adjusted both of these elements, with the hope that the Orc will now feel better enabled to find impact throughout a match.

War Anthem [Augment]:
- [Bugfix] Physical Power Aura and March activation now grant Assists when they buff an Ally Hero.

March [Primary]:
- Healing increased from 10/15/20/25/30 to 14/21/28/35/42.
- Healing Magical Power Scaling increased from 10% to 15%.

Song Of My People [Secondary]:
- Cooldown decreased from 2s to 1.4s.

N3on’s general strength is on the high-end right now, but at times feels difficult to access and comes with the requirement of a deeper mastery of her mechanics to truly start unlocking her potential. While there is nothing inherently wrong with this, there are elements of her Kit that skew her strength too heavily to competitive play such as her i-frame on dash, while also serving as a hard counter to too many matchups and Heroes in general. As N3on is already rather elusive and effective when mastered, we’re removing the i-frame to bring greater matchup parity and remove some of this competitive skew, which thereby allows us to inject strength further into L.I.N.X and offer it more consistency with its bounce-back cadence without it breaking the bank.

Dox [Augment]:
- Bonus Magical Power decreased from 8% to 5%.

L.I.N.X [Primary]:
- Damage increased from 40/60/80/100/120 to 45/65/85/105/125.
- Magical Power Scaling increased from 45% to 50%.
- Cost decreased from 55/65/75/85/95 to 50/60/70/80/90.
- Max Range decreased from 1950 to 1825.
- Bounce Back delay decreased from 0.5s to 0.25s.

Data Burst [Secondary]:
- Magical Power Scaling decreased from 75% to 70%.

Erase Vector [Alternate]:
- Damage decreased from 70/100/130/160/190 to 70/95/120/145/170.
- No longer provides damage immunity during the dash.
- Projectiles no longer pass through N3on while dashing.
- N3on can now be hit by Crowd Control such as Stun and Knockup effects whilst dashing.

Now that Phase’s Energy Lane can be body blocked, the increase in the stacks to root was a little overkill, making it too difficult for her to navigate the laning phase and find impact against wily opponents. As a result, the stack counter is returning to 8 (at the cost of some Slow to ensure it can still be juked to a degree), returning her previous cadence now that there is more counter-play present.

Energy Lance [Secondary]:
- Slow decreased from 3.5% to 3%.
- Slow Stacks to Root decreased from 9 to 8.

Competing for the throne of the Junglers, Rampage is another Hero that has found great success since the v1.12 update. Now that he has transitioned away from feeling like as much of a bruiser and far more durable, his general damage output still remains too high. This damage primarily comes from his Rumbling and Tiny Titan Augments respectively, pushing him far over the edge when paired with his new tools and durability. As a result, alongside some general hits, both of the aforementioned Augments are receiving some heavier tuning to bring him back to further parity.

Tiny Titan [Augment]:
- Total Attack Speed decreased from 50%/55%/60% to 40%/45%/50%.

The Rumbling [Augment]:
- Rumble Damage decreased from 30/55/80/105/130 to 30/50/70/90/110.
- Total Physical Power Scaling decreased from 35%/38%/41%/44%/47% to 32%/34%/36%/38%/40%.

General:
- Health Growth decreased from 113 to 109.

Rumble [Secondary]:
- Slow Bonus Health Scaling decreased from 0.5% to 0.4%.

Behemoth [Ultimate]:
- Bonus Healing per Enemy Hero decreased from 10% to 8%.

While generally strong, landing a Riplash in the early stages of the lane can often result in Riktor losing out on trades due to its limited damage profile. As part of his general loop, it stands to reason that if Riktor lands a well timed hook on the correct target he should generally be rewarded through pressure, health advantages, and general all-in threat. As this is infrequently the case in the early lane, a small damage bump is needed to Riplash.

Riplash [Alternate]:
- Damage increased from 5/40/75/110/145 to 10/45/80/115/150.
- Max Health Damage increased from 8% to 9%.

Shinbi’s new All-Kill, currently results in excessive amounts of pressure. Not only does it simply deal a bit too much damage currently, but the duration at which she can bank her stacks and tag a member of the enemy team should they get hit by the one stray wolf can result in too many multikills. To ensure that more precision is required, and that opponents have a better window to recover from her barrage of wolves, reductions to the general uptime of Line Tempo and All-Kill are needed, better ensuring that Shinbi can still access these pop-off moments, but in a way that is more reasonable for her opponents to interact with.

Line Tempo [Primary]:
- Cooldown increased from 5.5/4.75/4/3.25/2.5 to 6./5.25/4.5/3.75/3.

All-Kill! [Ultimate]:
- Damage per Wolf decreased from 44/72/100 to 44/68/92.
- Magical Power Scaling per Wolf decreased from 18% to 16%.
- Stack Duration decreased from 8s to 6s.
- Mark Duration decreased from 8s to 6s.

Skylar’s Hypercharge currently cuts through opponents a little too quickly, especially in the later stages of the lane after she has levelled it up a couple of times. While the ability definitely needs to deal damage to be satisfying, there are too many cases of 100-0 that occur too frequently in the early game, making it overly difficult for opponents to interact with her regardless of her choice in engagement. Due to this, a large hit to its damage, as well as a touch less range while using Air Assault are being levied to ensure her matchups feel more skillful. In return, she is receiving an increase to the uptime of Plasma Grenade, better enabling her to choose to max out either ability, based on her playstyle and build preferences.

Plasma Grenade [Primary]:
- Cooldown decreased from 13/12/11/10/9 to 13/11.75/10.5/9.25/8.

Air Assault [Alternate]:
- Bonus Basic Attack Range decreased from +125 to +100.

Hypercharge [Alternate]:
- Damage decreased from 1/3/5/7/9 to 1/2.5/4/5.5/7.
- Total Physical Power Scaling decreased from 10% to 9%.
- Bonus Attack Speed Scaling decreased from 11% to 10%.

The potency of Steel’s 1-2 punch and general damage output is too high given his durability. We’re slowing down the rate and lethality of his basic attacks and Shield Bash to better ensure his damage profile is more in line with a Tank and less oppressive to deal with.

General:
- Physical Power decreased from 56 to 54.
- Attack Speed decreased from 140 to 135.

Shield Bash [Alternate]:
- Damage decreased from 50/90/130/170/210 to 50/85/120/155/190.

TwinBlast is currently struggling to find impact relative to other Carries. As one of the goals of his v1.12 changes was to lean into his identity as a gunslinging, highly mobile Carry, we’re further increasing this aspect of his gameplay by offering him more uptime and ability potency, better enabling him to dash around fights and find impact with his arsenal of abilities to contrast the downside of being a Carry with shorter range.

Vaporize [Primary]:
- Bonus Physical Power Scaling increased from 80% to 85%.
- On-Hit Modifier increased from 140% to 150%.

Rocket Dash [Secondary]:
- Cooldown Refund On-Hit increased from 5%/6%/7%/8%/9% to 7%/8%/9%/10%/11%.
- Cooldown Refund against Non-Heroes increased from 2%/2.4%/2.8%/3.2%/3.6% to 2.8%/3.2%/3.6%/4%/4.4%.

Vortex Grenade [Primary]:
- Cooldown decreased from 11/10/9/8/7 to 10/9/8/7/6.
A quick bugfix for Wraith, no longer allowing his Knock, Knock to unintentionally pierce through Towers now that it also no longer pierces Terrain.

Knock, Knock! [Alternate]:
- [Bugfix] No longer pierces Towers.
- [Bugfix] No longer pierces Towers when Mystic Marksman is active.

The Monkey King is struggling to find his place in the v1.12 ecosystem, feeling a little bit left behind relative to the strength of the rest of the roster. He especially feels less threatening than many of the other Assassins and Skirmishers, with his general mana economy and burst output being too low for him to function relative to the more potent Junglers. Some adjustments are needed here that will better allow a tricky Wukong to find success throughout a match once they bring him closer to the general baseline of other Heroes.

General:
- Mana Growth increased from 44 to 48.

High Impact [Body - Secondary]:
- Damage increased from 60/95/130/165/200/235 to 60/100/140/180/220/260.

Yin’s general damage output and lifestealing potential reaches an overly powerful breakpoint in the later stages of a match once her items are online and all the compounding effects kick-in. Once she reaches this state, it leaves little room for response from opponents, especially when that level of damage and sustain is paired with her strong disruption tools. To remedy this, some general late-game damage reductions for her Basic Attacks are in order, better ensuring she remains a strong scaling threat, without it being as oppressive.

Silksong [Basic Attack]:
- Bonus Physical Power Scaling decreased from 85% to 80%.

Yurei’s general success in the hands of a player that has mastered her remains too high, with her general elusiveness, survivability, and damage output all being too high. Reductions to these areas are needed to provide her opponents with more room to counter and disrupt her flow, should she opt into a poor engagement or overly aggressive position

General:
- Movement Speed decreased from 690 to 685.

Anima Burst [Primary]:
- Healing Bonus Physical Power Scaling decreased from 90% to 80%.
- Missing Health Healing decreased from 70% to 60%.
- Cooldown increased from 11 to 12.

Severance [Secondary]:
- Bonus Physical Power Scaling decreased from 120% to 110%.

Zarus’ general flexibility and wide toolkit, paired with the general shift to the v1.12 ecosystem have landed him as one of the primary threats in the Jungle. Due to the breadth of tools he has available to him, his general effectiveness needs to be reduced across the board, with his general durability and regenerative lizard-skin properties receiving notable hits to ensure he cannot stay as healthy and present on the map between skirmishes.

General:
Health Growth decreased from 117 to 113.
Attack Speed Growth decreased from 2.2 to 1.8.
Physical Armor Growth decreased from 4.55 to 4.2.
Movement Speed decreased from 695 to 690.

Gladiator [Passive]:
Healing decreased from 0.4%/0.8%/1.6%/3.2% to 0.3%/0.6%/1.2%/2.4%.
Nyrian Spear [Basic Attack]:
Bonus Physical Power Scaling decreased from 80% to 75%.

Evade [Secondary]:
Mana Cost increased from 50 to 50/55/60/65/70.
Cooldown increased from 13/12/11/10/9 to 13/12.25/11.5/10.75/10.

Coliseum [Ultimate]:
Bonus Physical Power Scaling decreased from 120% to 110%.
Cooldown increased from 140/115/90 to 140/120/100.

With the increased potency of various Heroes that utilize shields, such as a Gideon armed with Azure Core and Soulbearer, the need for a more direct anti-shielding strength increases. Therefore, we’re increasing the Anti-shielding of both Demon Edge and Astral Catalyst to better ensure that there is a more appropriate check within the item system when too many shields are present on one team.
- Demonic Bonus Damage vs Shields increased from 40% to 45%.

While Gaia Greaves bridges the gap between Fighter and Tank, it often feels most oppressive on mobile Fighters that can pair the durability and mobility it offers with their own aggressive tools while the Tenacity offered allowed them protection from being locked down by CC. As Tanks care less about Tenacity due to their innate durability, we’re opting to reduce the amount offered on Gaia to specifically target a reduction in efficacy for various Fighters that utilize it too well.

Salvation exists to provide various Melee Fighters with a form of heavy temporary durability to offset incoming bursts in the later stages of a match once enemy damage becomes higher and the need to dive into the enemy team head-first is more present. With the strength of various damage-based classes once they achieve 3-4+ items, Salvation’s shielding effect can stand to gain a small bump to better provide these Fighters with a durability spike that can match the incoming damage.
- Aegis Shield Max Health Scaling increased from 18% to 22%.
- Event Horizon Bonus Damage vs Shields increased from 40% to 45%.

Since its shift in statline now making it more potent and accessible, the Mana Regeneration capabilities of Hexbound are too potent, with it transcending the line of “heavy mana regeneration” to “infinite mana” too heavily. As a result, it is seeing a reduction.

- Mana Restore against Heroes decreased from 20% to 15%
- Mana Restore from Non-Heroes decreased from 8% to 5%.

Elafrost struggles to compete for its slot for the Heroes that should be best suited for it, relative to the strength of other Tank items such as Fire Blossom and Tainted Guard. Some additional Physical Armor is being granted to close that gap.

And that’s it for this one! We’re excited to hear what you think of these changes - please do let us know. The next balance update is coming soon on March 24th, so don’t hesitate to flag anything that stands out.
Thank you again for all your feedback since V1.12!

In a world where ancient magic intertwines with feudal tradition, a champion of light walks a dark, perilous path. Raised in the ways of combat by her grandmother, Scarlett grew to become a sworn servant of the people, a champion of justice whose kindness is matched only by her mastery of the blade.

For years, her path was clear: defend the helpless and serve as a beacon of hope for those in need. But when a dark, tragic fate struck her beloved, cursing him with a beastly burden, her life was irrevocably altered.

Refusing to let the darkness claim the one she loves, Scarlett now travels the land seeking a cure for his dark curse. Guided by her inquisitive nature and an unyielding knowledge of the wilds, she walks a perilous road between light and shadow. Armed with a blazing spirit, her precise rapier, and a chain lantern to light the way, Scarlett stands ready to illuminate the battlefield and destroy anyone who threatens the innocent.

Effect: Scarlett twirls in her current movement direction, with its speed increasing based on current momentum. Scarlett then stabs forward 3 times (610u range), with each dealing 21/31/41/51/61 (+24%/28.5%/33%/37.5%/42% Total Physical Power) Physical Damage to all Enemies in the area. The final stab deals up to 100% bonus damage based on the Target’s Missing Health.
Stabs benefit from Lifesteal and can Critically Strike at 60% effectiveness.

Effect: Scarlett winds up over 0.6s before thrusting forward (825u) with her Lantern, Restraining (Uncleansable Stun) the first Enemy Hero hit for 1.4s, and Slowing nearby Enemies within a 600u radius by 65% for 1s.

Enemies within a 600u radius of the Restrained Target take 100% of the strike’s damage.

Afterwards, Scarlett’s Blade is Ablaze for the next 8/10/12s, granting her +150 Basic Attack Range, +5 Energy Regen, and +20/32/44 (+12% Bonus Physical Power) Physical Power for the duration. Additionally, Empowered Cindara and Minueta are empowered to deal more damage during this time.

Effect: Swan Song marks the Restrained target. If they die within 8/10/12s, Ablaze extends by 5s, and a fiery zone appears beneath the dead target for 5s that heals Yourself and Allies by 100/150/200 (+65% Bonus Physical Power) each second.

Effect: Enhanced Cindara leaves behind a rupture that erupts after 0.5s. The eruption deals 20 (+4 per Level) (+25% Bonus Physical Power) True Damage to all Enemies in the area and Slows them by 40% for 1.25s.

Brawl returns! Shiny, new, and very much improved thanks to your feedback! We’ve made some changes to the ruleset, buffs and the map itself.

For those of you that are new to Brawl, it is a fast-paced, 5v5 gamemode where each team has a ticket score that gets reduced each time a Hero dies, Minions die, or when Minions are pushed into the enemy team’s portal. Be the first team to get the Enemy’s Ticket Score to zero to win!

For its return, not only has the Brawl map received some changes to its layout and visuals, but various mechanics have also been switched up that aim to make the mode more fun and resolve some of the pain points raised from its previous iteration.
The full details can be found below in the Brawl Mechanics Breakdown section, but the major points to note are:

- Win Condition: When a Team reaches 50 Tickets, Minion Deaths no longer reduce the Score. Only Hero Kills and Minions entering a Portal can reduce Tickets below 50.
- Orb Prime: Orb Prime no longer spawns in the middle of the map at 10-minutes.
- Lane Fangteeth: No longer appear each time a team has 5 Hero Deaths.
- Giant and Jump Height Buff: The Brown and Pink Golems have been removed and replaced by Cyan Buffs, with New Buffs now being present in the middle of the Map!
- New Buffs: Instead of Orb Prime and Lane Fangtooth, there are now 2 Buffs that appear on either side of the map, spawning every 2-minutes. The Buffs are a range of new Giant Golems that provide powerful effects to the killer's team by collecting a Buff Orb, such as super speed, increased size, Double-Ultimate, and more!
- Primal Fangtooth: Will now also appear at one of these New Buff Spawn Locations, every 2nd spawn. The Team that kills the Primal Fangtooth will now have it spawn on their side of the map, with it charging down the Lane towards the Enemies Portal, scoring a large amount of Tickets if it makes it into the Enemies Portal!
- Multiple Heroes On The Same Team: Heroes are once again limited to 1-per team, meaning you can no longer play 5 of the same Hero on the same team. However, we will enable multi-hero selection for special dates and events, so keep an eye on our socials!
Known Issue: Replays do not currently work for Brawl Mode.

- The game ends when a team's tickets reach Zero.
- When a team has only 50 tickets remaining, minion kills no longer reduce tickets.
- Only Hero kills and Portal kills reduce tickets at sub 50 Tickets.

- Orb Prime has been removed from Brawl.
- Lane Fangteeth no longer spawn based on Player Kills.
- Purple and Orange Buffs have been removed and reworked into a new Random Buff Giant.

- Killing an Enemy Minion -1 Ticket from Enemy Team.
- Pushing an Allied Minion into the Portal -1 Ticket from Enemy Team.
- Killing an Enemy Lane Fangtooth -1 Ticket from Enemy Team.
- Pushing an Allied Lane Fangtooth into the Portal -25 Tickets from Enemy Team.
- Killing an Enemy Hero -8 Tickets from Enemy Team.

- Each team has access to two Cyan buffs on their side of the map.
- In the center of the map there are new contestable buffs.
- One side has a Random Giant Buff spawns every 2-minutes.
- The other side starts with a Random Giant Buff then a Primal Fangtooth spawns alternating every 2-minutes (every other spawn).

- Killing it spawns a Lane Fangtooth for the team that secured the kill. It does not provide the Primal Buff in Brawl.

Four new Eternals are joining the fray in this update! We always envisioned this system to be expandable, and seeing such a great community response to the first release, we wanted to bring some more in to keep build diversity and customisation fresh.

- Damaging an Enemy Hero below 30% Health fires 4 (+1 per 30% Bonus Attack Speed) projectiles that each deal 8 (+1 per level) True Damage and apply on-hit effects at 100% Effectiveness (8s CD per Hero).

- Forage: Gain 4 additional Gold and 4 additional XP per Minion or Monster kill.
- Dryad's Boon: Basic Attacks decrease basic ability cooldowns by 0.2s on-hit
- Natural Resistance: Cleanse all crowd control and gain 400 Tenacity when below 25% Maximum Health. (Cleanse: 20s CD)

- Wind-Rider: Gain 20% Total Attack Speed for 4s after using a Dash, Leap, Teleport or upon leaving Stealth.
- Barkskin: Deal 3 (+1 per Level) Physical Damage to Enemy Heroes that Basic Attack you. This Damage triggers On-Hit Effects at 50% effectiveness. (1s CD)
- Taproot: Basic Attacks restore 1 (+8% Bonus Physical Power) Health On-Hit.

- Attacks and abilities against Enemy Heroes apply a stack of Rust for 5s. Each stack shreds 2% (+0.2% per Level) Physical Armor and Magical Armor, stacking up to 4 times. You gain 75% of the Armors Shredded.

- Frequency: Gain 2% Total Attack Speed and 2 Ability Haste per Rust Stack currently applied.
- Patina: Gain a 30 (+15 per level) Shield when not taking damage for 12s. Gain 4% Movement Speed whilst the shield holds.
- Dampening: Incoming damage from enemies farther than 1100 units away is reduced by 12%.

- Peal: Gain 25 Ultimate Ability Haste. Upon casting your ultimate, attacks and abilities apply maximum stacks of Rust for 4s.
- Fracture: Deal 4% (+0.3% per level) more Damage against targets with maximum stacks of Rust.
- Resonant Repair: Whenever you are Immobilized, you restore 3% of your Maximum Health over 4s.
- Decrease your size by 10%. Upon casting an ability, nearby enemy Heroes within a 600u radius are debuffed, causing them to deal 4% decreased damage for 3.5s, stacking up to 3 times.

- Bioluminescence: Enemies you damage take 3% bonus Damage and are Revealed for 4s.
- Harmonic Currents: Casting an ability restores 2.5% of your Missing Health and Missing Mana.
- Diffusion: Increases the radius of Pilow's Debuff Pulse by 50% and the duration by 1.5s.

- Neurotoxin: Pilow additionally increases damage enemies take by 2% per stack.
- Convection: Gain 4 Physical Armor and 4 Magical Armor for every active stack of Pilow on nearby enemy Heroes.
- Lil Sucker: Basic Attacks steal 2% of the target's Movement Speed for 3s, stacking up to 3 times.

- Takedowns grant a stack of Fearless, up to a maximum of 6 stacks. Your Max Health is permanently reduced by 5% (+4% Melee/+6% Ranged per Fearless). Gain 5% (+5% per Fearless) increased Physical Power, Magical Power and Attack Speed. Fearless is reset upon death.

- Demonic Bargain: Gain 350 additional Gold at levels 1/7/13.
- Risen: When at 3 or more Fearless stacks gain 12% Omnivamp.
- Hellfire Strikes: Basic Attacks deal 3 (+1.5 per level) True Damage On-Hit.

- Broken Wings: Your Movement Speed cannot be altered by item or abilities.
- Rite: Abilities cost an additional 5 (+2.5 per Level) Health to cast but you permanently gain 15 (+1 per Level) Ability Haste.
- Psychosis: Deal 3.5% (+0.4% per Level) more Damage to the closest Enemy Hero but 10% less Damage to any other Enemy Hero.
- There is a new sound effect when you fall to Critical Health (-25%), that should be more distinct and less panic inducing.
Practice Mode has had the following adjustments and additions:

- Haste Capsule now refreshes all Cooldowns when activated.
- There is a new Capsule to Evolve your Crest a stage per hit.
- There is a new Capsule to fully stack stacking Items and/or add some stacks to infinite stacking Items.
- Once the Camp Leader of a Normal Jungle Camp is killed (2/3/4/5 Camp), the remaining Monsters will now despawn after 10s of not being in combat.

- Enemy Fountains no longer 1-shot you upon entering their Zone.
- Upon standing in the Enemy Fountain’s Zone, you now receive ramping true damage instead.
- There is a new Camera Lens Effect & SFX to signify when you enter the Enemy Team’s Fountain.

- Certain abilities (such as Boris Ultimate, Ranged Basic Attacks, Melee Basic Attacks, Bayle Ultimate, and Crunch Empowered Right Crunch will no longer yoink you back or hit you if you manage to get a small distance away from the original location, such as by blinking out of their path.

- Ally and Enemy Heroes now cast a shadowy decal beneath their location on the ground when they are in the air.
- This will make it easier to tell where Flying Heroes such as Howitzer and Wukong precisely are when they are above you, as you will be able to see their shadow directly below them on the ground.
- Respawned Inhibitors now show a purple material around them to signify they are disabled and do not attack, adding more clarity.

- Mini Prime now drops its buff on the floor slightly in front of it when it dies, rather than being granted to the killer. The Buffs last for 30s on the floor.
- The first Ally Hero to walk over it gets it. Enemy Heroes cannot pick it up but it will appear greyscale for them at the location.

- From 20:00 onwards, Red & Blue Buff now drop an ADDITIONAL Buff Pickup at their original spawn location, that lasts in the world for 30s.
- The first Ally Hero to walk over it gets it. Enemy Heroes cannot pick it up but it will appear greyscale for them at the location.
- Red & Blue Buff are now a slightly different Color when Buff Dropping is active (at 20:00).
- In other words, Junglers can now kill their Buffs late-game, and let an Ally pick up an additional copy of that buff.

- Tier 1 Outer Tower Platings no longer disappear at 13 minutes and are now present for the entire match.
- Tier 2 Inner Towers now also have Tower Platings for the entire match.

- Ground targeting abilities now aim directly from the Camera reticle, rather than from the Hero’s model. This will reduce the amount of times an ability clips against a wall unintentionally.
- Ground targeting abilities now place at the centre of your reticle, rather than being slightly offset to the left.
- Aim Assist for Controllers has been adjusted to be slightly less sticky, while improving other areas of it that should make the gameplay experience smoother for Controller Users.

We're approaching the final stages of development, and this patch introduces a significant number of gameplay and map updates, alongside the first environmental dressing pass using existing assets.

Please note: This is not the final dressing pass - far from it. Everything included in this update is completely placeholder work intended to improve the map for the upcoming tournament while larger-scale visual improvements are still in progress.

- Duo Lane Adjustments
- Mid Lane Adjustments
- Jungle Adjustments
- Pit Adjustments

The primary goal of this initial dressing pass is to shift the map's focus away from its current visual simplicity and toward capturing the overall feel and atmosphere of Sanctuary. This pass is intended to establish the right mood and gameplay readability while we continue making core map changes.
A complete visual overhaul and final dressing pass will take place once the gameplay layout has been finalized.

On Saturday August 15th & Sunday August 16th, a 2-day Daybreak Invitational Tournament is happening. This will feature 8 Teams composed of the Top Players from NA PCC Summer!

This event will showcase the Daybreak Map in a more high-stakes environment, allowing us to gather deeper feedback on all things Daybreak as the best players from the North American Region put it through its paces!
For the Format, it is a Player Draft Event, meaning 8 Captains have been pre-selected from the Top NA PCC Summer Teams, who then draft the rest of their squad from the remaining PCC Player pool.
The Teams are competing for the grand prize of $1,000 and representation within the Daybreak Map when it fully releases, as well as additional Platinum Prizes of 50K & 25K for 2nd and 3rd place!

Finally, a Devs vs VennyVens (Reigning EU PCC Summer Champions) showmatch will be kicking off the event, so be sure to tune in to see if the VennyVens have what it takes to bring down the people’s champ, RGSACE!

- Saturday 15th August - [10am ET / 4pm CEST]: Dev Showmatch + Top 8 Swiss Bracket.
- Saturday 16th August - [10am ET / 4pm CEST]: Top 4 Double-Elimination Finals Bracket.

- Four New Eternals added.
- Reductions to the strength of Basic Attacks for the majority of Ranged Heroes at Level 1, thereby reducing the strength of Ranged Offlaners.
- Recalls are no longer interrupted by DoT Damage.
- Red/Blue Buff now drop a 2nd Buff on the Floor for the killing team after 20:00.
- Mini Prime now drops its Buff on the floor for the killing team, instead of granting the Buff to the Killer.
- Rivers/Blue/Cyan now grant Energy Regen on Kill.
- [Bugfix] Various Stacking Shred Effects now work correctly instead of capping out after the 1st instance of Shred.
- Hero Size now has a Max and Min Cap.
- Tower Platings no longer removed at 13:00.
- Tower Platings have been added to Tier 2 (Inner) Towers.
- Refillable Potions Heal less at Level 1.
- Ground Targeting Improved to be more accurate
- Heroes now display a team-colored Shadow beneath their location when in the air, making them easier to track.
- Enemy Fountain no longer 1-shots you, and instead deals ramping true damage the longer you stand inside of it.
- White Camps now despawn after 10s of being out of combat if the Camp Leader is killed.
- Respawned Inhibitors now have a Purple Material around them, better signposting they cannot attack you.
- Various Basic Attacks and Abilities should now no longer hit you/rubberband you back if you correctly Blink/Dash away from them (E.g: Boris Ultimate).
- Aim Assist Strength reduced slightly for Controller Users, but smoothened in other areas.
- Items now display a variety of new information and stats when hovered over on the Scoreboard.
- General outlier balance.
- And more!
- Aim Assist for Controllers has been adjusted to be slightly less sticky, while improving other areas of it that should make the gameplay experience smoother for Controller users.

Ever Blinked away from a Boris just to get grabbed by him despite your Blink cooldown being eaten? Or blinked away from a Crunch Uppercut just to get knocked up anyway? While this can still happen when accounting for higher Ping, these outcomes should happen FAR less, resulting in a smoother, and more skillful gameplay experience, as before Client-based prediction would overly-favour the Hero using the Ability to confirm a hit, rather than the Hero that successfully dodged it.

- Client-predicted Attacks such as Boris Ultimate or Basic Attacks will no longer hit you if you successfully Blink/Dash far enough out of their Range.
- In the case of certain dash abilities, (E.g: Boris Ultimate) when a successful dodge occurs, the attack will fail and now stop the attacking Hero at your previous location you blinked from.

Getting 1-shot by the Enemy Base is a little unintuitive and poorly signposted, while also just simply being less fun than having the chance to execute a celebratory dive when a match is about to end. Now, you can dive into the Enemy’s Fountain if you wish, and instead of being 1-shot, you will take heavy true damage that ramps up over time instead (most Heroes will die within 4-7s seconds at most, so it's not super easy to do).

- Enemy Fountain no longer 1-shots you.
- Now deals 50 (+4% Max Health) True Damage every 0.5s to you while in the zone. This damage increased by an additional 10 (+1.25% Max Health) Damage every tick, for a maximum of 130 (+14% Max Health) Damage each tick.
- Now Displays a Camera Lens Effect and plays an SFX when you enter the Enemy Fountain.

Ever been frustrated by accidentally firing a Ground Targeted Ability at a wall due to invisible collision?! Me too! With these changes, Ground Targeting will be more consistent and accurate to where you are actually aiming, resulting in additional precision and far less accidental mis-fires that were of no fault of the Player.

- Now Targets from the Camera, instead of the Hero Model, reducing the frequency of unintentional corner clipping when using Abilities such as Gideon’s Cosmic Rift.
- Now Targets from your Cursor correctly, instead of being slightly offset to the Left, making aiming more precise to the User’s actual intent.

Ever wondered how much damage your Combustion has dealt across a match? Or how useful a variety of other Items have been?! Well now you can tell by focusing the item on the Scoreboard. However, for this pass, not every Item could be covered just yet, but we are hoping to expand this functionality further in the future where possible!

- Various Items now display a range of statistics in-game, such as the damage they have dealt over the course of a match.
- You can view yours, or other Players’ Item stats, by hovering an Item on the Scoreboard.
- Stat tracking for other Items that were waived this pass (such as Tainted Items “Healing Reduced" and “Damage Blocked” by Shields) are on our list to do in a future update, as they are larger technical undertakings.
Heroes can now be more easily tracked when in the air (looking at you Wukong), as they now cast a clear shadow directly beneath them when they are in the air.

- Ally and Enemy Heroes now cast a shadowy decal beneath their location on the ground when they are in the air.
- Blue Shadow: Ally.
- Orange Shadow: Enemy.
- Inner Circle: Gets smaller the higher the Hero is in the air.

With the addition of various DoT effects into the game, such as Vesh’s Burn, we have decided to allow Recalls to go through even when affected by a DoT effect, as it is largely an obnoxious limitation that adds more frustration to gameplay than is necessary.

- Damage Over Time (DoT) Damage Effects no longer interrupt Recalls.
- Recall can now be cast immediately after taking damage, instead of having a 0.15s Cooldown.

Max/Min Size is being capped, helping resolve a variety of issues, including Camera issues on larger Heroes, and the strength of Heroes such as Tiny Titan Rampage who can become obnoxiously unfair to even try and hit when they are excessively small.

- Hero Max Size increase is now capped to 2.5x
- Hero Minimum Size Scale is now capped to 0.55x.

We are removing the ability to “dirty” a Jungle camp by leaving one alive, as this can lead to excessive snowball scenarios when abused in high level play, while being a generally unintuitive and unfun mechanic for the average player to engage with.
- Camps with multiple units (2/3/4/5 Camp) will now despawn after 10s of being out of combat if the Camp Leader is killed.

Blue and Red now drop an additional buff at 20-minutes when killed, meaning Junglers no longer have to forgo as much Gold and Experience when looking to hand off the Buff to an Ally Hero, and can still have one themselves! Oh, and it now grants Energy Regen, meaning it is valid for Energy Heroes to utilize!

- Now drops a second buff on the floor for 30s at the Buff’s original spawn location after 20:00 that can be picked up by a member of the killing team.
- The Red Buff Giant now changes color slightly after 20:00 to signify it will now drop an extra Buff.
- Blue Buff now also grants +5 Energy Regen.
A quick addition to Cyan Buff to ensure it has additional value for Energy Heroes like Scarlett.
- Now also grants the Killer 25% Max Energy Regen instantly.

Mini Prime now drops its buff on the floor at a fixed location when killed, meaning Junglers can now use their Hunt to secure the Buff without having to worry about how to hand it off to their Teammates. Be careful though, if you don't pick it up within 30s, it will disappear, meaning the Enemy Team has a chance to deny you even if you kill the Mini Prime!

- No longer grants its Buff to the Killer.
- Instead, upon dying, it now drops the Mini Prime Buff on the floor for 30s that can be picked up by a member of the killing team.
Like Blue Buff, Red Buff also drops an additional Buff at its spawn location when killed, post 20:00 game time!

- Now drops a second buff on the floor for 30s at the Buff’s original spawn location after 20:00 that can be picked up by a member of the killing team.
- The Red Buff Giant now changes color slightly after 20:00 to signify it will now drop an extra Buff.
A quick addition to River Buffs to ensure it has additional value for Energy Heroes like Scarlett.
- Now also grants the Killer +15 Energy Regen for 5s.
- Now also grants the Killer +25 Energy Regen for 5s.
Tower Platings no longer fall off at 13:00, meaning teams on the back foot still have a chance at claiming the standing gold and catching up, even when behind.

- Tower Platings no longer deactivate at 13:00, and now remain for the entire match.
- Tier 1 Plating Gold Reward decreased from 70 to 60.

Tier 2 Towers are also gaining Plates for the entire match, better allowing Tier 2 Pushes to result in some additional progress and gold gain, rather than it feeling like its not worth to even bother hitting a T2 Tower if you can't kill it in any single push (while also helping to slow down the rate that a single Split Push can destroy them, thanks to the Bonus Armors that Plates provide when destroyed).

- 4 Tower Platings added on each Tier 2 Tower. They remain for the entire match.
- Tier 2 Local Gold On Kill decreased from 400 to 250.
- Tier 2 Plating Gold Reward = 50.
The confusion around whether an Inhibitor is “fake” or not is now a problem of the past! Once an Inhibitor respawns, it will now be a different color, making it easier to spot at a glance.
- Respawned Inhibitors now display a Purple Material, better highlighting to Players that they cannot attack.

Cauterize is one of the least-used Blessings, and clogs up the Vermis Blessing set in such a way that it makes mix-ups in its 1st category way too restrictive for Ranged Users. As a result, we are removing it and replacing it with a new Blessing: Mechadrive.
Mechadrive is replacing Cauterize, offering a range of Heroes, from Twinblast to Boris, a new option to consider when running Vermis instead of being bound to Serration as hard.
- [New] Basic Attacks reduce your Secondary Ability’s Current Cooldown by 10% On-Hit. Reduced to 5% against Non-Heroes.

Marrow is receiving a soft rework, with it no longer allowing its User to heal off of Minions Waves. Now, Marrow’s Healing is loaded far more into Hero Combat, meaning its users cannot win the lane by default by simply taking a trade and healing off the Minion Wave. In return, AoE effects now heal for 65% Effectiveness, instead of the 33% Effectiveness imposed on Omnivamp, making the Eternal more useful to a range of Heroes in general, despite being a relatively similar strength in early-game skirmishes.
- [Soft-Rework] Heal for 6%/7%/8%/9% of damage dealt to Heroes, increased up to 15%/20%/25%/30% based on your Missing Health. (65% Effectiveness for AoE Attacks. 15% Effectiveness against Monsters).

Roses is receiving two changes: Firstly, it now has a cap on the amount of bonus gold it can offer, as previously it provided its Users with far too much Gold in snowball scenarios and led to absurd economic outcomes. Secondly, the previous Hero Kill Omnivamp Amplification Effect from Marrow is being granted to Roses, providing it some additional payoff now that the Gold has been limited.

- Bonus Takedown Gold is now capped at +100g (5 Takedowns).
- Hero Kills now also grant +50% Effectiveness of Marrow’s Major Blessing for 8s.
Ferocity is receiving another hit to the amount of Attack Speed it offers, in order to slow down the rate at which it ramps up and becomes oppressive when utilized by Ranged or DoT Heroes alike.

The King provides a significant amount of excess gold income, especially in various Range vs Melee matchups when it can be stacked relatively safely, and contributes too heavily to snowball scenarios. As a result, it is seeing a reduction.
- Gold on Basic Attack decreased from 7 to 6.
We’re undoing the previous nerf to Nihil, as it continues to be one of the weaker performing Eternals.
- Stat Effectiveness per Takedown or Level increased from 18% to 20%.

Feeding Frenzy provides a surprising amount of Attack Speed in a fight considering how little thought its Users must put into their position. We’re reducing its radius to ensure that Heroes must actually position with purpose and sit amongst a group of targets to get its full effect, rather than it incidentally tagging everyone in a fight with ease.

Immaculate continues to cause excessive stat-check scenarios, both in the early-game and in the late-game. Another reduction is required in the short-term to ensure laning dynamics and 1v1 interactions between Heroes are not warped as easily.

Masterpiece results in rather significant snowballing for the User’s that can leverage it reliably, such as Feng Mao, and Eden. A reduction is occurring to make a single kill less-overbearing to deal with in a fight.

Aion is another Gold generation Eternal that is providing too much value and warping the Economy curve of the average match too heavily - often resulting in lane performances being irrelevant when playing against it. Another reduction is occurring to make sure it is less universally useful, and more tailored to the Heroes that can reliably trigger it.
- Gold Gained From Ability Damage decreased from 7% to 6%.

Sacrifice is being reworked, as previously it was providing far too much free Mana Regen in the laning phase, allowing the likes of Shinbi and Argus to cheat the lane entirely with near-infinite Mana Pools simply from hitting the Wave. Now, Sacrifice User’s have to actually interact with their opponent and are rewarded by engaging in aggressive gameplay loops, preserving laning dynamics in a healthier manner.
- [Reworked] Damaging an Enemy Hero with an Ability grants 2.5% Missing Mana Regeneration over 5s. Hero Kills regenerate 20% Missing Mana over 5s.

With the previous round of changes to Akeron and him now possessing additional utility and damage from his Health Scalings, we’re looking to normalize his build options further by reducing the general strength of his Magical builds, as they are currently far overperforming his Tank or Physical alternatives.

- Magical Power Scaling decreased from 18% to 16%.
- Hero Missile Homing Radius decreased from 450u to 380u.

- Web Shot Magical Power Scaling decreased from 40% to 35%.
- Leap Magical Power Scaling decreased from 40% to 35%.
- Bite Magical Power Scaling decreased from 45% to 40%.

The previous round of changes to Argus were made to elevate the areas of his kit that were generally lacking, and to be in line with the other changes that happened to the majority of Mage’s across the class. With that now past us, we are reducing the general strength of his Particle Shredder, as well as heavily limiting the amount of free Mana he can restore throughout the lane by simply hitting Minions thanks to the changes to both his Augment and to Aion’s Sacrifice, better ensuring there is an appropriate Mana:Damage tradeoff when he’s looking to pump a target.

- No longer restores Mana when hitting Non-Heroes.
- Mana Restored when hitting Heroes increased from 10% to 12%.

- Damage decreased from 13/20/27/34/41 to 13/19/25/31/37.
- Magical Power Scaling decreased from 18% to 16%.
- Mana Cost changed from 12/14/16/18/20 to 13/14/15/16/17.
- Cooldown increased from 3 to 3.5.

Countess was one of the few Mages last patch that did not really receive a great benefit from the changes. For this pass, we’re pushing her late-game Ultimate Damage and Durability up slightly to bring her further up to speed, as the teamfighting stage of the game is where she starts to struggle to find windows for execution.

A quick bump to Crunch’s lesser used Augments, with Lunge Crunch returning to old values to better enable his Jungle play patterns, and Falcon Crunch offering some additional bang for its buck to better match the strength of the others.

- Empowered Right Crunch Damage increased from 15% to 20%.
- Empowered Right Crunch In-Air Cooldown decreased from +30% to +25%.

Dekker is the first Ranged Hero receiving a reduction to her base Physical Power, thereby reducing the strength of her early-game poking capabilities and creating a larger gap between the raw damage output of a Ranged Hero compared to a Melee Hero. The reason is largely the same for other Heroes with this style of change, so context will be skipped for other Heroes for the sake of time.

While it may not appear as much of a damage loss on the surface, the damage loss adds up over the course of a lane, and better enables Melee Heroes to posture into a Ranged Hero and close the distance. It should be noted that the changes are more heavy handed for Heroes that are more likely to appear in off-roles like Offlane, and in some cases the Physical Power loss is being returned through additional Growth to ensure that Carries especially still feel functional and with agency once the mid-game rolls around.

- Physical Power decreased from 60 to 57.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 3.6 to 3.8.

Alongside the Physical Power reductions described in Dekker’s Context section, Eden is receiving a shift to her Focal Lens Augment once again, as it can result in too much proportional Cooldown Reduction, and therefore too much Tachyon Lance spam in the late-game, especially when paired with items like Solaris. Instead of a flat reduction, it is now a percentage, normalizing the value to be far healthier in these cases.
- Tachyon Lance Cooldown Refund changed from 1s to 10% Total.

- Physical Power decreased from 53 to 49.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 3.8 to 4.
- Heat Generation Modifier decreased from 20%/35%/50%/65% to 12.5%/30%/47.5%/65%.

As a followup to the previous Feng Mao changes, we are now making some targeted changes to reduce the strength of Feng Mao at higher-ranks. The previous change helped normalize his clear and allow him to function a little more freely in the early-game, and now we’re looking to strip back some of this damage away from his Isolation Damage as it can result in too much abnormal burst and is best utilized by experience players. Likewise, his Ultimate Reset Timer is seeing a reduction, as in high-skill lobbies, a single reset results in too much pressure for too long of a period as it allows Feng Mao to skirt the outside of a fight with ample time to find the perfect window.

- Isolation Damage decreased from 25/36/47/58/69 to 25/35/45/55/65.
- Bonus Physical Power Scaling decreased from 30% to 25%.

Gadget is the first of a handful of cases where Shred Effects have not been functioning correctly, resulting in a significant loss in utility. This has been occurring since v1.14, and with it now resolves, we expect to see all affected Heroes and Items perform far better than before, and will be monitoring their performance moving forward.
Greystone was also affected by the Shred Bug, meaning he was only shredding Armor once, rather than 4 times. This has now been resolved.

Ikra is receiving a soft-rework to his Cascade Augment, as it continues to provide too much raw value with Items such as Oathkeeper, and is railroading his builds too hard to the point it has created a Balance Bottleneck due to how bound he is to those Items to succeed. Now that it no longer allows Brine to apply On-Hit effects, Ikra’s general strength can be better observed and tuned moving forward.

- No longer applies On-Hit Effects.
- [Reworked] Basic Attacks grant a stack. At 5 stacks, the next direct Brine hit deals 10 (+20% Magical Power) bonus damage. Ability hits grant Ikra 12% Attack Speed stacking up to 4 times (once per ability).
- Magical Power Scaling decreased from 50% to 45%.

Some Base Physical Power reduction for Iggy to diminish his strength further in the Offlane, in-line with the changes to other Ranged Heroes. And a quick bugfix that was resulting in him dealing an extra tick of damage with his Passive under specific circumstances.

- Physical Power decreased from 52 to 49.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 3.9 to 4.1.
- [Bugfix] Fixed an issue where Badlands Critter could deal double damage if Iggy Ignites a Target with a single stack on them.
Khaimera’s Unleash has suffered from a few bugs causing it to feel unresponsive and desynced. These have now been resolved.

- [Bugfix] Khaimera increased attack speed no longer liners after the effect ends.
- [Bugfix] Khaimera’s Basic Attacks should no longer feel desynced while Unleash is active or hitting a target after it has finished.

- Physical Power decreased from 21 to 20.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 1.6 to 1.65.

Alongside the general reductions to early game Physical Power, Morigesh’s Spirit Shred Augment was another case that was impacted by the Shred Bug causing only 1 instance of reduction to occur. This has now been resolved.

- Physical Power decreased from 52 to 50.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 3.8 to 4.

- Physical Power decreased from 58 to 55.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 3.8 to 4.

- Physical Power decreased from 54 to 52.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 3.4 to 3.55.
Narbash’s Percussive Tear was another instance of the Shred Bug occurring, and has now been resolved.
- [Bugfix] Fixed an issue where N3on could re-cast Final Thread while Rooted.

Alongside the general Physical Power reductions for Ranged Heroes, Phase is also receiving a large change to her Psychic Flare, with it no longer reducing her Blink Cooldown as Heavily. This will allow her opponents a far better chance at catching her out and locking her down in fights, especially in higher level play where this mechanic is utilized far more aggressively.
- Blink Cooldown On Hit increased from 1s to 2.5s.

Tiny Titan continues to stand out as Rampage’s premier Augment as it is seeing a reduction in the general shrink it provides. The reason for this is that Tiny Rampage affords him a form of pseudo-durability due to being so hard to hit, especially when paired with Krix and other Shrink effects, making him near impossible to deal with once he’s on top of a target. Combined with the Minimum Size Cap described above, Tiny Rampage should be a lot more manageable to strike down in a fight, and feel far more fair to fight against.
Some small but meaningful buffs for Riktor, aimed at increasing his general success in the Offlane and Jungle Roles now that he has been afforded some additional early game damage and clear speed.
- Damage per Level increased from 4 to 5.
- Pulse Damage Modifier increased from 50% to 75%.

Shinbi, much like Argus, benefits too heavily from engaging in passive gameplay loops that can be difficult for opponents to disrupt or interact with. In her case, she has historically been heavily tuned around a limited Mana Pool to ensure that she cannot sit back and farm passively with Line Tempo with too much ease, but with various new forms of Mana Sustain entering the game since the addition of Eternals, this is even less so the case. As a result, we are adjusting her Line Tempo to deal reduced damage to Minion waves after it hits a Minion, reducing the rate at which she can blast through Minion Waves at Level 5+. In return, Line Tempo itself is receiving a damage increase, making it stronger as a dueling tool that she can leverage in aggressive trades.

- Upon hitting a target, the Wolf now deals 60% damage to Minions that are hit afterwards.
- Damage increased from 70/105/140/175/210 to 85/125/165/205/245.
- Magical Power Scaling increased from 55% to 60%.

- Physical Power decreased from 57 to 54.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 2.4 to 2.55.

- Physical Power decreased from 61 to 57.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 3.4 to 3.6.
- Max Health Damage decreased from 0.3% to 0.25%.
- [Bugfix] Fixed an issue where Steel could Blink during his Ultimate.

Terra’s Axe Retrieval has been underutilized for a while now, with it not really providing enough raw value to justify its use. To open up some additional playstyles, it now grants her Highland Hurl some additional damage, thereby allowing Terra to consider a more axe-orientated playstyle.
- Now also grants Highland Hurl +15% Damage.

- Physical Power decreased from 57 to 55.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 3.2 to 3.35.

While TwinBlast is receiving the general Physical Power changes that are occurring to all Heroes, the previous hit to Solaris impacted his general strength so we are granting him back some Ability up-time to ensure he can keep up with the rest of the Carry Roster

- Physical Power decreased from 66 to 63.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 4.3 to 4.5.

- On-Hit Modifier increased from 150% to 170%.
- Cooldown changed from 12.5/11/9.5/8/6.5 to 13/11.25/9.5/8.25/6.

- Physical Power decreased from 60 to 57.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 3 to 3.2.

Offlane Zinx has been causing a stir as of late, with her general ability to both run down and escape opponents being too high. For this pass we are taking some more aggressive swings at her Offlane viability especially, with her now boasting a lot less poke damage and outright durability in the early-game, and a far longer window between Triage Protocol activations.
- Additional DoT Damage Dealt decreased from +50% to +35%.

- Health decreased from 685 to 670.
- Physical Power decreased from 50 to 46.
- Mana decreased from 340 to 320.
- Mana Regen increased from 1.75 to 2.
- BAT increased from 1.35 to 1.4.
- Cooldown increased from 17-4.25 (-1.75 per Level) to 24/17.5/11/4.5 at Levels 1/6/11/16.

With the reduction to Basic Attack Damage for many Heroes in the early-game, we can now more comfortably reduce the amount of free sustain provided by Potions in the early game, without having to fear excessive snowballing scenarios occurring as much by doing so.

With the addition of Satariel and its Demonic Bargain Blessing, we’re bumping up Lucky Feather’s Cost and Sell value by 50g to prevent players from purchasing it from match start as we deem that it would be an unhealthy strategy to allow.

- Cost increased from 700 to 750.
- Sell value increased from 400 to 450.
Ruthless Broadsword is another case of the Shred Bug occurring, essentially resulting in it, and both Viper and Basilisk respectively, Shredding no Armor. This has now been resolved.

Ashbringer was suffering from a bug that prevented certain multi-hit Basic Attack Damage from triggering its effect more than once per attack/burst, making it lose over half its value on certain Heroes. This has now been resolved.
- [Bugfix] Now correctly Triggers its Cooldown Refund Effect multiple times for Attacks such as Skyler’s Hypercharge, and multi-hit Basic Attacks such as TwinBlast and Lt. Belica.

Manta Scythe has seen a surge of play as of late, with it offering both a strong outlet of sustain, late-game scaling, and general burst potential. To ensure the Item does not cover too many bases, too strongly, we’re opting to drop its isolation damage once again, as this aspect of the Item’s effect can lead to excessive burst scenarios that go against the more sustained-fighting nature of the item.
- Divide & Conquer Isolation Damage decreased from +10% to +8%.
A quick hit to Omen’s Cooldown Refund, as currently it is contributing to excessive uptime for certain Ability Combos.
- Bestial Momentum Cooldown Refund decreased from 25% to 20%.

Augmentation has largely fallen out of favour in the recent months, with it struggling to keep up with other Items in its Class, especially since the adjustments to Physical Power across the Carry/Assassin/Fighter Classes in 1.14. Some additional Physical Power and a slight cost reduction is therefore being granted to bring its efficiency up to more relevant levels.

- Cost decreased from 3150 to 3100.
- Physical Power increased from 30 to 35.

Berserker’s Axe is another Fighter Item that doesn’t pull its weight in the damage department, and is struggling to serve its function as an aggressive roaming item for those that use it best. A small bump in its damage potential and sticking power are required to bring it back into contention.

- Physical Power increased from 40 to 45.
- Health decreased from 300 to 275.
- Blitz Slow decreased from 50% to 45%.
- Blitz Slow Duration increased from 0.75s to 1s.

Mutilator’s Basic Attack Effect is now having its damage extended to all Target Types, providing Junglers with an alternative choice alongside Manta Scythe and Sky Splitter for a sustain-focused 1st buy, as previously the lack of PvE damage made the Item feel like it had too high of an opportunity cost to consider.

- Mutilate now applies its Basic Attack Effect against Minions & Monsters.
- Mutilate Damage is capped at 20 against Minions & Monsters.

Rebirth continues to provide a little too much general value and uptime to its Users. Once again the effect is seeing a bump down in its general efficacy, alongside an increase to its cooldown to make it less universally present throughout a match.

- Cost increased from 2950 to 3000.
- Health decreased from 300 to 275.
- Mechanica Cooldown increased from 240 to 270.
- [Bugfix] Fixed an issue where it was possible to Blink during the Rebirth Resurrection state.
Magnify is the final Shred Effect that was affected by the aforementioned Shred Bug, making it only apply 1-stack of Shred. This has now been resolved.
Cursed Scroll continues to provide too much raw damage output when paired with Krix, and is seeing another reduction in its potency to bring it down to a healthier middle-ground.

- Curse Of Pain Damage decreased from 30 to 20.
- Forbidden Art Attack Speed decreased from 2.5% to 2%.

- Major Blessing: Additional Stats per Stack decreased from +12% to +10%.
- [Bugfix] Major Blessing: Now grants 2 stacks at Match Start as the Player starts the Match at Level 3.

- Major Blessing: Damage decreased from 1% to 0.75%.
- Major Blessing: Ability Haste decreased from 4 to 3.
- Major Blessing: Movement Speed decreased from 0.75% to 0.6%.
- Major Blessing: Max Health decreased from 1.5% to 1.2%.

- +3% Damage Dealt.
- -6% Damage Taken.
- +10 Ultimate Haste.
- Brawl now generally has the same gamemode specific balance changes to Heroes, Items and Eternals as ARAM.

- Passive Small Entity Drop Chance was 50% now 90%
- Passive Minute Threshold was 7 now 7.
- Passive Stacks Below Threshold were 8 now 10.
- Passive Stacks Above Threshold were 6 now 8.
- Passive Gains 1 Stack every 12s.

- Tiers stacks were 40/80/120/160 now 35/70/105/140
- Passive Gains 1 Stack every 10s

- Fixed an issue where, during Ranked Draft, on Dawn Team the second User could lose their Hero Selection upon the first user locking in their pick.
- Fixed an issue where Users could receive a placeholder Crest Screen if they had a removed Crest in their Loadout, such as Earth Spirit (RIP).
- Fixed an issue where Narbash’s Ultimate Mesmerize could trigger multiple Immobilize events, instead of just once.
- Fixed an issue where Users would be unable to change their Eternal if they had an invalid Augment selected.
- Fixed an issue where Green Buff’s Explosive Shield would not state its name in the Death Recap.
- Fixed an issue where the Gifting Button could flicker if hovered during Battlepass previews.
- Fixed an issue where a User’s selected Eternals could be swapped out to Default when swapping Roles in Draft.
- Fixed an issue where Changing Mode would display the ARAM pop-up, despite it being outdated.
- Fixed an issue where Controller Users were unable to navigate the Post-Match Scoreboard.
- Fixed an issue in Ranked Draft where, after picking a Hero to Ban, if the Ban does not go through, the Hero would still be highlighted and blank.
- Fixed an issue where AFK Players would be required to Vote during a Surrender Vote.
- Fixed an issue where Users would be unable to Basic Attack or Use Abilities if they Disconnect from a Match while using the Free-look function.
That’s it for this update! We can’t wait for you to get your hands on it - let us know what you’re most excited for on our Discord and Reddit!
Game Design and Community @ Omeda Studios
