It wouldn't be Shadow's Eve without a map makeover! Sanctuary has well and truly been petrified, complete with haunting new lighting, jack o' lanterns, candles and more!

As mentioned last patch, we wanted to assess the strength of Weald’s Major Blessing after reducing the strength of its Minor Blessings. Now that we’ve seen the results, the Major Blessing continues to provide too much burst damage to Heroes, so a reduction in strength is needed - especially in the case of On-Hit effect interactions.

- Missile Base Damage decreased from 8 to 7.
- Missile On-Hit Modifier decreased from 30% to 20%.
Taproot continues to provide too much value to its users, making Weald too well-rounded as a total package. Another reduction in the Healing it offers is needed to bring it further in line.
- Bonus Physical Power Scaling decreased from 7% to 6%.

Cannibalism can contribute to some niche, but powerful snowball scenarios when early Takedowns are achieved. To help reduce the amount of mid-game durability available for its users that get ahead, we’re trimming down some of its value.
- Max Health on Takedown decreased from 30 to 25.

Feeding Frenzy is currently contributing to the damage output of Bruisers that run Krix a little too heavily, resulting in Bruisers opting for Krix over alternatives such as Thraex due to there not being enough of a damage tradeoff relative to other, less durable Eternals.

Patina’s Shield has received more appreciation from players thanks to the long-term effective health it provides its user throughout the laning phase, as well as the anti-burst it offers as the late-game rolls around. We’re reducing the strength of the shield slightly at all stages of the game, making it less oppressive to play into.
- Shield decreased from 35-290 (+15 per Level) to 30-268 (+14 per Level).

Dampening has largely flown under the radar as a significantly strong defensive option against long-range opponents. Now that players are beginning to realise its strength, it’s time for us to tone it down so that it is more in line with other defensive Minor Blessings that offer a similar benefit.

Lotus continues to blur the lines between offense and defense as a catch-all Eternal thanks to the variety of stats it offers. While this is largely part of the Eternal’s identity that makes it accessible to a range of Heroes, for Mages and Bruisers especially, it is providing too much durability in combination with the rest of its effects. As a result, we’re pulling down the Health on offer, ensuring there is a greater durability tradeoff for Lotus compared to other tankier Eternals.

Immaculate continues to contribute to unhealthy all-in stat check scenarios, both in the early lane, and in late-game catch scenarios. Once again we are reducing the DR, and will monitor it further to assess if larger changes become necessary.

We have seen a rise in the uptake of Philosopher on Heroes such as Shinbi and Countess that simply seek to accrue gold throughout a match, allowing them to freely scale up and accelerate. Given that Heroes do not need to interact with opponents to benefit from Philosopher and is therefore low risk, it is simply granting too much free gold.

Aurora’s wall has been suffering from 2 bugs. Firstly, it was not granting Movement Speed to Allies on the wall at all. And secondly, there was a rather destructive bug where Aurora could split off the lane to block Minions, which would then cause them to retreat back up the lane, and sometimes even all the way back to the Inhibitor. Naturally, this was rather OP. Alas, both have now been resolved.

- [Bugfix] Fixed an issue where Aurora’s Wall would not grant herself or Allies Movement Speed while on the Wall.
- [Bugfix] Fixed an issue where Aurora could force Minions to path back up the lane when blocking a lane with her wall. They will now walk into it and stop correctly.

Bayle is receiving a range of changes aimed at providing him the uptime, durability, and damage he needs to function as a Bruiser in late-game scenarios. Currently, he tends to fall off a little too hard in the mid-game and beyond unless he secures a large snowball, which results in Bayle players frequently opting for 1-shot Assassin builds to feel useful, rather than a more well-rounded Fighter build. We hope that these changes provide him with the tools he needs to feel functional when investing in more durable Fighter builds, as the additional durability should now provide his base kit strengths the time to shine across longer fights.

- Attack Speed Growth increased from 1.4 to 1.8.
- Physical Armor Growth increased from 4.8 to 5.2.
- Movement Speed increased from 690 to 695.

- Bonus Physical Power Scaling increased from 80% to 85%.
- Magical Power Scaling increased from 50% to 55%.

- Damage Taken Healing increased from 10%/14%/18%/22%/26% to 10%/15%/20%/25%/30%.
- Mana Cost increased from 60 to 60/65/70/75/80.

- Bonus Physical Power Scaling increased from 110% to 125%.
- Cooldown decreased from 17/15.5/14/12.5/11 to 16/14.5/13/11.5/10.
- Mana Cost increased from 40 to 40/45/50/55/60.

The previous round of changes to Drongo helped bring him back into the spotlight as a serious contender in the Carry role. However, we are currently not too happy with his ability to rip Rad Rounds and run at his opponent in early all-in scenarios, so we are reducing his level 1 durability and damage by a smidge to ensure he has to choose his engagements a little more wisely.

- Physical Power decreased from 57 to 56.
- Health decreased from 695 to 680.
- Physical Armor decreased from 27 to 26.
- Magical Armor decreased from 29 to 28.

To help bring further utility and reinforce her unique elements, we’re bumping up the speed of Gadget’s Security Gate, and increasing the Shred on offer from her Ultimate. These changes will make catching opponents or speeding Allies a little more reliable, while also solidifying her strengths as a strong anti-tank Mage, compared to the rest of the roster.
- Max Range Travel Time decreased from 1.35s to 1.2s.
- Magical Armor Shred increased from 3.5% to 4%.

After investigating Greystone further, we continue to feel like he is providing too much value at higher levels of play when it comes to acting as a neutralizing force, that then transitions into a sticky diver in the end-game. As a targeted nerf to higher levels of play, we’re reducing the amount of refund he gains when leaping on an Enemy, as this is a skill-check high end players hit more consistently, and therefore benefit from more frequently.

- Cooldown Refund on Hero Hit decreased from 35% to 30%.
- [Bugfix] Cooldown refund now only occurs on Hero or Camp Leader hit, as stated.
We’re making some smaller changes to Grux’s ability to take all-ins and repeat trades in the early game thanks to his Basic Attack strength, and Double Pain’s lower Mana Cost.

Ikra has gained a surge of popularity in high-end play, thanks to his offering of incredible safety, scaling, and late-game burst potential. Now that players are starting to master Ikra and utilize his mechanics to their fullest, we are looking to make some targeted changes to the strengths that the best Ikras take advantage of (Gold Scaling, Zoning with Stuns, Ultimate 1-shot combos), and offering him a little strength on his lesser used Eternal Passives and Cascade Augments to ensure there is still variety in playstyle for him while not hitting Ikra’s viability on the lower end as heavily, as he already struggles to make an impact when controlled by the average player.

- Damage increased from 10 to 15
- Magical Power Scaling increased from 20% to 30%.

- Harbinger Fathom Magical Power Scaling increased from 8% to 10%.
- Divine Bubble Healing increased from 4/6/8/10/12 to 5/8/11/14/17.
- Divine Bubble Healing Magical Power Scaling increased from 10% to 12%.
- Gold On Kill decreased from 3/4/5/6/7 to 3/3.5/4/4.5/5.

- Damage decreased from 320/480/640 to 320/460/600.
- Slow decreased from 50% to 40%.

While winrates alone might lead some of you to believe Khaimera is overly powerful, when you dig beyond the simple numbers, it is clear that Khaimera feels rather dysfunctional and weak right now, especially in mid/high tier play. As a simpler Hero with limited options to outplay an opponent, he needs a higher general level of strength to function and feel satisfying. While we are conscious of not inflating Khaimera's strengths too heavily in lower tiers of play where he thrives, we believe he has room for improvement due to his inability to stick to targets with his leap, or survive easily once the later stages of a match roll around. As a result, we are targeting some early game nerfs towards him to slow him down, as this is typically where he feels most oppressive for lower tiers of play due to isolated fights, and then reinforcing his ability to stick in ganks, and survive in the late game with Armor Growth improvements that will compound with the Regeneration he possesses.

- Physical Power decreased from 65 to 63.
- Physical Armor decreased from 35 to 30.
- Physical Armor Growth increased from 3 to 4.

- Bonus Physical Power Scaling increased from 70% to 80%.
- Slow changed from 25%/30%/35%/40%/45%/ to 40%.

Kwang is receiving a round of changes aimed at bringing greater consistency to his Tether + Ultimate combo, as oftentimes by the time the player has realised they hit a target and begin channeling their Ultimate, the target is already free from the tether. Alongside this, we are granting him some smaller damage and utility increases to make him feel appropriately spiky at level 6 (his Rank 1 Ultimate can feel underwhelming), and ensure he has adequate damage output in late-game scenarios when he is committing to bulkier builds.

- Damage increased from 230/340/450 to 250/360/470.
- Slow increased from 45%/55%/65% to 50%/60%/70%.

The previous round of adjustments to Belica’s Seismic Assault and Combat Veteran Augment have provided her with new levels of consistency that have pushed her strength over the edge. While we are generally pleased with the result of making her more enjoyable to play, she now needs to lose some general strength to compensate for the new-found consistency. While most of this is coming from her Combat Veteran Augment when combined with other sources of XP stacking such as Orb or Lotus, there is still room to trim some burst damage and uptime away from her kit to ensure that there are more appropriate tradeoffs when building that style. Likewise, we have tuned Combat Veteran’s XP to be less powerful after roughly Level 8, meaning Support Belica can still feel good about choosing it to keep up in early levels, but Mid Belica will no longer accelerate up 2-3 Levels as easily in the late-game.

- Movement Speed decreased from 3% to 2.5%.
- Passive XP decreased from 0.1-3 to 0.1-2.
- Ability Haste per Maxed Ability decreased from 10 to 8.
- Magical Power Scaling decreased from 20% to 17.5%.

Murdock continues to trail behind other Carries due to his weaker early game compared to the more aggressive Carries such as Revenant and Drongo. While they are receiving hits to their power which will naturally make Murdock’s strength more valuable, we are pushing 1 more set of smaller changes to give him the additional stats he needs to hold his own in the early lane, and transition into a more stable mid-game.

- Physical Power increased from 55 to 57.
- Health Regen increased from 1.35 to 1.5.
- Attack Speed Growth increased from 1.4 to 1.6.

Renna has faltered ever since her last set of hits she received to her Ultimate. While we stand by those changes, she is currently struggling to keep up with the stronger Mages. To help provide her with more conditional pop-off moments, we’re granting her Mortal Coil some additional damage and execute capabilities, allowing her to better work down her opponents and threaten a satisfying kill with its use.

- Damage increased from 70/100/130/160/190 to 70/105/140/175/210.
- Magical Power Scaling increased from 50% to 60%.
- Execution Threshold increased from 6% to 8%.

Revenant has risen to the pinnacle of the Carry role, possessing incredible pressure in the early game and the ability to snowball out of control should his opponents make but 1 or 2 mistakes. While snowballing is a part of his identity we’d like to somewhat maintain, we are undoing some of the previous buffs to his 4th Shot Movement Speed and Ultimate Cooldown, while also dropping his general damage output and snowballing to more appropriate levels by trimming back his trading power, late-game scaling, and the dueling potential his Ultimate’s Stat Steal effect provides.
- Bonus Physical Power decreased from 3%-13.2% (+0.6% per Level) to 3%-11.5% (+0.5% per Level).
- Fourth Shot Movement Speed decreased from 12% to 10%.

- Cooldown increased from 135/120/105 to 140/125/110.
- Stat Steal decreased from 8%/9%/10% to 6%/7%/8%.

Now that Scarlett players have mastered her further, she can now receive some reductions to her general strength back closer to her initial release strength. Given her Energy economy and general combat loop’s cadence, she is a difficult balance case as there is a fine line between making her too weak in conventional scenarios, or overpowered with too many winning matchups. Given this, we’re making some smaller changes to her ability uptime and early durability, alongside reducing the Critical Damage present on her Minueta to reduce the strength of Terminus/Solaris builds in the early game. These changes should help normalize her matchups in Offlane further, and potentially open up more skill-matchups/soft-losing matchups for her to be concerned about navigating, but keep her feeling impactful to play.

- Physical Armor decreased from 36 to 35.
- Health Regen decreased from 2.2 to 2.

- Cooldown increased from 7/6.25/5.5/4.75/4 to 7.5/6.75/6/5.25/4.5.
- Critical Strike Modifier decreased from 60% to 50%.

Sevarog is receiving a range of quality of life changes to his general hitboxes and ability feel. While these changes are certainly power-positive, we feel Sevarog can feel a little clunky at times, especially in the case of his Ultimate’s hitbox being too tight, and how his Siphon can feel awkward to weave in combination with his Basic Attacks, and is therefore deserving of the changes simply to make him feel more enjoyable and intuitive to play. Oh and there’s some Junglerog buffs, yay!

- Bonus Monster Damage increased from 30/35/40/45/50 to 40/45/50/55/60.
- [QoL] Cast Frame decreased from 7.5 to 6.
- [QoL] Animation Speed increased from 1.2x to 1.3x.

- Range increased from 375 to 425.
- [QoL] Cone Angle decreased from 130 to 120.

Shinbi continues to be a menace with her high dash uptime and ability to rain sparkly havoc across late-game teamfights with her Ultimate. To combat this, we’re reducing her Allegro Augment’s Cooldown refund to ensure she’s a little bit easier to lock down and catch, while also reducing some of the late-game strength of her Ultimate, as it currently kills too many Heroes from excessively high health thresholds when she gets a few items online.
- Rushing Beat Cooldown Reduction decreased from 20% to 15%.

- Damage decreased from 44/68/92 to 44/66/88.
- Magical Power Scaling per Wolf decreased from 16% to 15%.

Terra continues to feel underwhelming for many. Once again we are increasing the power of her Highland Hurl, as this is the ability that can feel the most lackluster to use, both in terms of damage and utility. By shifting around the scaling from Slow Duration to Shred, we’re now granting her more agency in Skill Order based on matchups - as she typically struggles to deal with Tankier opponents as she is unable to access Penetration/Shred Items due to her Armor Scalings. Likewise, the utility of her Slow/Root is now more powerful, better allowing her to control fights and contribute to her team as a disruptive frontliner, even when behind.

- Bonus Physical Armor Scaling increased from 30% to 40%.
- Bonus Magical Armor Scaling increased from 30% to 40%.
- Physical Armor Shred increased from 20% to 20%/22.5%/25%/27.5%/30%.
- Slow Duration increased from 1/1.05/1.1/1.15/1.2s to 1.25s.
- Root Duration increased from 1/1.05/1.1/1.15/1.2s to 1.25s.

The Fey has flown under the radar for a while now as an incredibly powerful pick, and avoided adjustments despite other Mages around her falling down in strength. To ensure that she doesn’t rise above everyone else, we’re dropping the safety offered by Bramble Patch’s Movement Speed slightly, while also reducing her mid-game harass from her Harvest Nettles (those things hurt).

Similar to Murdock, TwinBlast has largely been suppressed by the likes of Revenant and Drongo. While we are mindful not to push his strengths too high, there is slightly more room to give him some love in the ability department, better opening up some On-Hit and Assassin build paths and providing him with additional build variance.

- Bonus Physical Power Scaling increased from 90% to 95%.
- On-Hit Modifier increased from 170% to 200%.
- Total Physical Power Scaling increased from 40% to 45%.

Valmont has taken a while for players to get used to, but now that they better grasp his kit and mechanics, it has become apparent that he is simply too powerful and in need of a power cut in various areas.

To provide a little more context and transparency on his strength, when we tested him internally prior to release, we saw many players heavily struggling to succeed with him in their initial 5-10 matches despite us believing he was powerful in the right hands (which was mirrored by players struggling in the first week of his release too). This is typically normal - especially with more unconventional Heroes. As a result, with many new Heroes we tend to give them slightly more power than necessary as a way of compensating for the mastery curve players must go through when learning to play as, with and against a new Hero over the initial release patch, with players becoming more competent with each match they play towards the next balance update. In Valmont’s case, we definitely overshot a bit too much. While there is no exact science to this as it's difficult to predict the speed players will become proficient with a new Hero in various skill brackets, hopefully that helps explain why some Heroes can release as seemingly “OP” - especially in Valmont’s case, as we already predict he will trend to being stronger in lower skill-brackets due to the healing/spacing checks he places on opponents that can lead to him feeling oppressive, similar to Khaimera.

There is a fine line between us overshooting and the Hero being too strong, or undershooting and everyone giving up on it after a couple of matches, thus diminishing the impact of a new Hero’s release because players feel it's too underwhelming to stick with. Overall, it's an important (but challenging) aspect of nailing the Player Experience that we must consider for new Hero releases that will always have mixed results, but hopefully this insight is helpful in allowing you to understand the balance process a little further!

- Omnivamp Bonus Mana Scaling decreased from 0.5% to 0.4%.
- Hero Death Bonus Mana decreased from 30 to 20.
- [Bugfix] Updated the Description to state that Valmont must kill targets to gain Mana, now matching the existing functionality.
- Missing Health Damage Modifier decreased from 100% to 85%.

- Mana Restore On Unit Kill decreased from 3-41 to 3-38.
- Lilith Damage decreased from 15/23/31/39/47 to 12/20/28/36/44.

- Damage decreased from 20/29/38/47/56 to 20/28/36/44/52.
- Cooldown increased from 8/7.5/7/6.5/6 to 9/8.5/8/7.5/7.

- Damage decreased from 40/70/100 to 40/65/90
- Damage Magical Power Scaling increased from 22% to 23%.
- Healing decreased from 25/45/65 to 20/40/60.
- Healing Magical Power Scaling increased from 20% to 22%.
Arise my Wukong brethren! Hair stacks no longer fall off over time, meaning your Clones will be up more consistently, and you can feel less bound to his Masterful Mimicry Augment.
- Wukong no longer loses Hair Stacks while Out of Combat.

Yurei’s Skulls have been suffering from a bug where they were counting as Minions for the sake of various interactions, meaning effects that would boost damage against Minions would deal excessive damage when damaging them. This has now been resolved.
- [Bugfix] Fixed an issue where Yurei’s Skulls counted as a Minion for the sake of damage calculations and item effects.

Similar to some other Heroes such as Grux, we’re slightly nudging down Zarus’ early strength, specifically targeting his clear speed and level-6 gank potency from his Ultimate in order to slightly drop his efficacy and reduce how oppressive and impactful he can feel throughout the early game.

- Damage decreased from 200/325/450 to 180/305/430.
- Bonus Physical Power Scaling decreased from 100% to 90%.
- [Bugfix] Fixed an issue where various automatic basic attacks (Legion, Eden) would only stack the Crest on the first shot.

Exodus has seen a surge in popularity in the North American region especially, with players now fully seeing the power it has at disrupting fights and catching opponents. As a result, we’re undoing one of the Cooldown buffs it received in the past to ensure its uptime and ability to interrupt key abilities as frequently is reduced.

- Cooldown increased from 90 to 100.
- [Bugfix] Fixed an issue where Exodus’ Active Effect could not be used while Grounded/Rooted.

Rift Walkers has largely fallen out of favour ever since we reduced the range of its Pull. As it has been a rather long time since this occurred and the game has shifted dramatically since then, we are undoing that change, pushing it back closer to its old value (650) to bring it back into relevance. If it’s an overshot, we will adjust it as necessary in the following patches.
- Rift Snatcher Pull Radius increased from 550 to 625.

Quiver is another item that has largely fallen out of favour compared to other options, and given the amount of beefy frontliners running around, we want to push its strength up to give Carries a stronger countermeasure when dealing with close range divers.
- [Bugfix] Fixed an issue where Mutilator was not being applied on AoE abilities when they dealt damage to multiple enemies.

Azure Core is seeing too much popularity, even on Mages where its acquisition is questionable. To create a greater differentiation between it and other options, we’re dropping its Ability Haste, making the likes of Oathkeeper and Soulbinder more attractive first buys, alongside the staple of Combustion.
A quick bump for Oathkeeper’s effect damage, helping it better compete as an early game pickup.
- Celestial Spellblade Damage increased from 60 to 65.
Soulbinder continues to be underbought by the Heroes best suited to it, and is in need of a small bump to help it compete with the other 1st buys in the class.
- Arcane Salvo True Damage increased from 7% to 8%.
A quick bump for Luxforge’s Physical Power, as it has been left behind the other items that received a bump.
Flux Matrix is another item that sees minimal play. A bump to its Haste will make it more attractive relative to other Magical Armor items for the likes of Aurora, Shinbi and Kwang.

Vainglory can often feel a bit underwhelming to pick up, despite it signalling its use as a capstone. We’re granting it more strength to make it a more satisfying pickup for Armor stacks, and incentivise them to forgo a less durable damage item.

- Magical Armor increased from 35 to 40.
- In Vain Bonus Max Stack Armors increased from +10% to +12%.
Bottomless Vial suffered from an issue where it was granting more Magical Power than we intended in the 3v3 mode. This has now been resolved.
- [Bugfix] Magical Power per River Buff decreased from 15 to 5.
Recall Speed is being reduced in Crucible to improve the overall pacing of the mode.
Sevarog and Renna were not gaining stacks passively as they do in other game modes. This has now been implemented into Crucible.
- [Bugfix] The following Heroes now correctly gain Passive Stacks: Sevarog, Renna.
Items such as Overlord or Azure Core were not receiving stacks passively as they do in other game modes. This has now been implemented into Crucible.

- [Bugfix] Various Stacking Items now passively gain Stacks (E.g: Overlord), like they do in ARAM.
- [Bugfix] Various Crests Stacking Items now gain multiple charges per use (E.g: Obelisk), like they do in ARAM

We’re removing the custom damage modifiers from Crucible. These modifiers were originally designed around the 5v5 ARAM experience and did not translate well to the 3v3 environment, resulting in some Heroes having unintuitive power spikes, be that excessive damage or durability. Heroes will now be using their standard live values instead of having additional Damage Amps/Reduction Modifiers, and we hope this change provides a more consistent experience. We’ll be monitoring this change closely as the goal is to allow all Heroes to be playable and find success in Crucible, but this may cause some fallout. Naturally, we’re open to re-introducing custom values if it’s needed in future, but for now we’ll assess how the mode plays without them.
- Heroes no longer have adjusted Damage Output, Healing/Shielding Output, and Damage Taken modifiers in Crucible 3v3, and their stats now match their defaults.

We’re adding a small delay before Jungle Monsters spawn on match start. The goal of this change is to reduce the immediate rush at the start of the game and allow players more time to navigate the shop without the threat of the Enemy team taking Jungle Buffs before you’ve had time to even move.
- Various Jungle Monster’s Initial Spawn Time increased from 00:05s to 00:20s (See below for full details).

Small adjustments to Blue Buff that aim to decrease its damage potential in the early game whilst increasing the HP mid to late game to prevent the camp being cleared too quickly as the Heroes get stronger, and to be less punishing to kill solo.

- Health increased from 950 (+200 per Level) to 1000 (+300 per Level) at Levels 1-6, (+100 per Level) at Levels 7-11.
- Health Scaling now increases to Level 11 (increased from 6).
- Current Health Damage decreased from 6% to 4%.
- Initial Spawn Time increased from 00:05s to 00:20s.

Similar to Blue, Red will be receiving changes to decrease its damage potential in the early game whilst increasing the durability across the match. With this change, Red Buff will be able to take a few hits and allow teams more time to contest it before it’s killed.

- Health increased from 950 (+200 per Level) to 1000 (+300 per Level).
- Health Scaling now increases to Level 11 (increased from 6).
- Current Health Damage decreased from 6% to 4%.
- Initial Spawn Time increased from 00:05s to 00:20s.

Given how quickly they can be killed, River Buff spawning at the start of the match felt a bit disconnected from the intention of players fighting around the larger buffs. We’ve adjusted its initial spawn time to be slightly later than other Camps, meaning there is a better bridge in decision making between invading the Enemy River Buff, doubling back for your own, or going to the lane.
- Initial Spawn Time increased from 00:00 to 00:30s.
- Initial Spawn Time increased from 00:05s to 00:20s.
- Initial Spawn Time increased from 00:05s to 00:20s.
We’re reducing the duration of the Orb Prime buff to prevent it from influencing the game for an excessive amount of time, and give the defending team higher odds of making a comeback.
- Prime Buff Duration decreased from 180s to 150s.

The Fangteeth are receiving large amounts of changes aimed at reducing their damage potential and increasing their mid/late-game durability. We’re also reducing the stats gained from defeating Fangtooth, as the current rewards provide too much power and make it difficult for teams to recover after falling behind. Additionally we’ve adjusted its initial spawn to spawn later into the match to ensure players are strong enough to fight the demonic dinos.

- Fangtooth Current Health Damage decreased from 6% to 4%.
- Stats Gained per Fangtooth Kill decreased from 2% to 1.5%.
- Magical Armor increased from 25 (+1 per Level) to 25 (+2 per Level).
- Health increased from 3000 (+500 per Level) to 3000 (+625 per Level).
- [Bugfix] Health increased from 3000 (+500) at levels 1-11, then 16000 at 12-15, to 3000 (+625) at all levels.
- Initial Spawn increased from 150 to 210.

Marksman Crest was taking longer to charge on average than the other Crests, so we’ve reduced the stack limit required to Evolve. With this change the Crest will come online at a similar pace to other options.
- Stack Limit to Evolve decreased from 120 to 90.
- Stack Limit to Evolve decreased from 120 to 90.

- Fixed an issue where picking a Hero too fast would result in incorrect Eternals being assigned to the User.
- Fixed an issue where extra stats from Items and Augments were not being reflected correctly on the Shop Stats Column.
- Fixed an issue where Soulbearer was not granting its Shield on activation to Rage Heroes.
- Fixed an issue where Grim’s Instant Reload Augment would reset his Ultimate cooldown against targets that enter a Resurrection state.
- Fixed an issue with Lt. Belica’s Ultimate Description where it did not state there was a small forgiveness window on Hero Deaths resetting its cooldown.
- Fixed an issue where Eden’s Heat Bar would not visually reset after using her Ranged Ultimate.
- Fixed an issue where Steel’s Passive could result in a negative Armor value in specific scenarios.
- Fixed an issue where Valmont’s bats would remain active in the world after tracking an untargetable target.
- Fixed an issue where Pinging “Crest Ready” whilst on cooldown would incorrectly ping your Blink progress.
- Fixed an issue where Pinging “Blink Ready” whilst on cooldown would incorrectly ping your Crest progress.
- Fixed an issue where the Damage Hit Markers Reticule/Crosshair was not centralised on the screen.
- Fixed an issue where Orb Prime’s Buff VFX would not display if gained while Invisible.
- Fixed an issue where Yin was able to reflect other Heroes’ Projectiles whilst in Revenant’s Nether Realm.
- Fixed an issue where Gravitum and Voidgazer were not being reflected correctly in some scenarios.
- Fixed an issue where Gravitum and Voidgazer could destroy themselves if they were fired at each other.
- Fixed an issue where Scarlett’s Japanese Ability Descriptions could clip off the screen when levelled.
- Fixed an issue where Zinx DoT Damage was being shown as Infuse on the damage recap instead of Refibrillator.
- Fixed an issue where Wraith’s Sniper’s Bounty Augment would not add the Bonus Gold it generates to his “End Gold” on Scoreboard after a match ends.
- Fixed an issue in Replays where changing from Drone to Hero Chase will always result in the 1st Dusk Hero being selected.
That's all for now! Update v1.17.2 launches on Tuesday 13th October. Happy haunting!
Rei, Bronze & Steggs - Game Design & Community @ Omeda Studios
The Road to Paragon: Ranked in 1.18 and Beyond

Hey Champions!

A quick little hotfix has just launched to resolve the following:

- Fixed Valmont Emote having no VO 

- Fixed an issue with Valmont's Sanguine Banquet regenerating mana incorrectly 

- Fixed an issue with Valmont's Passive Description 

- Fixed an issue with the Crown Placement on Valmont's Unleashed skin 

- Fixed an issue with Victorious banner having incorrect drop shadow 

- Fixed an issue with Crucible wins not being tracked on Quests 

- Fixed an issue with Gideon's Black Hole pulling enemies if interrupted on cast 

- Fixed an issue with Gideon's Mana bar reflecting incorrect values on remote perspective 

- Fixed various issues with Localisation

Thank you for your patience!

[p align="start"]Hey Champions,[/p][p align="start"]It’s that time again, Update 1.17: Bloodtide is LIVE! We’ve got a bloodthirsty new Hero, one of the most highly requested game modes, and much more![/p][p align="start"]Let’s take a look…[/p][p align="start"][/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="ry5a2_AOrdc;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h2]New Hero: Baron Valmont[/h2][p align="start"]In a world torn by an endless war between the forces of the light and the shadow realm, Baron Valmont once served the light with honor as a high-ranking battle-mage. But when the Order's leadership fell to the corruption of its own power and turned toward tyranny, Valmont took up arms to lead a noble rebellion against them.[/p][p align="start"]The order retaliated with brutal cruelty. Consumed by grief, his desperate cries for vengeance echoed into the dark, reaching deep into the shadow realm. There, the blood goddess Lilith answered, offering him the powers of the night in exchange for an endless river of blood.[/p][p align="start"]Now bound to the ancient blade containing Lilith’s soul, Valmont has traded his humanity for unholy retribution. Wielding tragic fury and dark blood magic, Valmont enters the battlefield to bleed the corrupt dry and exact his brutal vengeance upon all who stand in his way.[/p][h3][b]Stats:[/b][/h3][quote][p]- Health: 685 (+133 per Level)
- Health Regen: 1 (+0.15 per Level)
- Mana: 400 (+60 per Level)
- Mana Regen: 1.3 (+0.2 per Level)
- Attack Speed: 125 (+1.7 per Level)
- Physical Armor: 28 (+5.7 per Level)
- Magical Armor: 29 (+1.15 per Level)
- Physical Power: 49 (+4 per Level)
- Movement Speed: 665
- BAT: 1.4[/p][/quote][h3][b]Abilities:[/b][/h3][p]Hemophagia \[Passive]:[/p][p align="start"][b]Effect:[/b] Your sword, Lilith, will attack the last nearby Enemy Target that is damaged by your Basic Attack, or Bloodbound, for 4s. Lilith deals 15 (+15% Magical Power) Magical Damage with each strike (increasing with Bloodbound’s Level).[/p][p align="start"]Lilith’s Attack Speed is equal to Valmont’s, and she attacks faster with additional Attack Speed. She returns to Valmont if she is not attacking a Target. She will teleport back to Valmont if he travels too far away from her.[/p][p align="start"]Additionally, Valmont restores 3-41 (based on Hero Level) Mana whenever an Enemy Unit dies within 1500u of Lilith. Hero deaths restore an additional 35% Maximum Mana.[/p][p]Crimson Sigil \[Basic Attack]:[/p][p align="start"][b]Type:[/b] Ranged[/p][p align="start"][b]Range:[/b] 1500u[/p][p align="start"][b]Effect:[/b] Ranged Basic Attack dealing 49 (+60% Bonus Physical Power) Physical Damage.[/p][p][/p][p]Rupture \[Primary]:[/p][p align="start"]CD: 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s[/p][p align="start"]Cost: 60/65/70/75/80 Mana[/p][p align="start"][b]Effect:[/b] Valmont manifests 5 blood-forged blades over his head. Over the next 0.75s, these blades sequentially launch forward 1600u toward his reticle, each detonating upon impact to deal 20/29/38/47/56 (+15% Magical Power) Magical Damage in a 300u radius.[/p][p]Bloodbound \[Secondary]:[/p][p align="start"]CD: 12/11/10/9/8s[/p][p align="start"]Cost: 40/50/60/70/80 Mana[/p][p align="start"][b]Passive Effect: [/b]Lilith’s Damage is increased by 0/8/16/24/32.[/p][p align="start"][b]Active Effect:[/b] Launch Lilith to a targeted location up to 1800u away, dealing 70/90/110/130/150 (+60% Magical Power) Magical Damage in a 325u radius and Slowing targets hit by 30% for 1.5s. Lilith will then target the closest Enemy and attack them for a short duration.[/p][p][/p][p]Arterial Grip \[Alternate]:[/p][p align="start"]CD: 16/15/14/13/12s[/p][p align="start"]Cost: 80/90/100/110/120 Mana[/p][p align="start"][b]Effect: [/b]Fire a Blood Tether 1600u that stops on the first target hit. The Tether deals 80/120/160/200/240 (+60% Magical Power) Magical Damage to the Target over 3s. Hey Champions,

It’s that time again, Update 1.17: Bloodtide is LIVE! We’ve got a bloodthirsty new Hero, one of the most highly requested game modes, and much more!

Let’s take a look…

New Hero: Baron Valmont

In a world torn by an endless war between the forces of the light and the shadow realm, Baron Valmont once served the light with honor as a high-ranking battle-mage. But when the Order's leadership fell to the corruption of its own power and turned toward tyranny, Valmont took up arms to lead a noble rebellion against them.

The order retaliated with brutal cruelty. Consumed by grief, his desperate cries for vengeance echoed into the dark, reaching deep into the shadow realm. There, the blood goddess Lilith answered, offering him the powers of the night in exchange for an endless river of blood.

Now bound to the ancient blade containing Lilith’s soul, Valmont has traded his humanity for unholy retribution. Wielding tragic fury and dark blood magic, Valmont enters the battlefield to bleed the corrupt dry and exact his brutal vengeance upon all who stand in his way.

Stats:

- Health: 685 (+133 per Level)
- Health Regen: 1 (+0.15 per Level)
- Mana: 400 (+60 per Level)
- Mana Regen: 1.3 (+0.2 per Level)
- Attack Speed: 125 (+1.7 per Level)
- Physical Armor: 28 (+5.7 per Level)
- Magical Armor: 29 (+1.15 per Level)
- Physical Power: 49 (+4 per Level)
- Movement Speed: 665
- BAT: 1.4

Abilities:

Hemophagia \
:

Effect: Your sword, Lilith, will attack the last nearby Enemy Target that is damaged by your Basic Attack, or Bloodbound, for 4s. Lilith deals 15 (+15% Magical Power) Magical Damage with each strike (increasing with Bloodbound’s Level).

Lilith’s Attack Speed is equal to Valmont’s, and she attacks faster with additional Attack Speed. She returns to Valmont if she is not attacking a Target. She will teleport back to Valmont if he travels too far away from her.

Additionally, Valmont restores 3-41 (based on Hero Level) Mana whenever an Enemy Unit dies within 1500u of Lilith. Hero deaths restore an additional 35% Maximum Mana.

Crimson Sigil \:

Type: Ranged

Range: 1500u

Effect: Ranged Basic Attack dealing 49 (+60% Bonus Physical Power) Physical Damage.

Rupture \
:

CD: 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s

Cost: 60/65/70/75/80 Mana

Effect: Valmont manifests 5 blood-forged blades over his head. Over the next 0.75s, these blades sequentially launch forward 1600u toward his reticle, each detonating upon impact to deal 20/29/38/47/56 (+15% Magical Power) Magical Damage in a 300u radius.

Bloodbound \:

CD: 12/11/10/9/8s

Cost: 40/50/60/70/80 Mana

Passive Effect: Lilith’s Damage is increased by 0/8/16/24/32.

Active Effect: Launch Lilith to a targeted location up to 1800u away, dealing 70/90/110/130/150 (+60% Magical Power) Magical Damage in a 325u radius and Slowing targets hit by 30% for 1.5s. Lilith will then target the closest Enemy and attack them for a short duration.

Arterial Grip \:

CD: 16/15/14/13/12s

Cost: 80/90/100/110/120 Mana

Effect: Fire a Blood Tether 1600u that stops on the first target hit. The Tether deals 80/120/160/200/240 (+60% Magical Power) Magical Damage to the Target over 3s. While tethered, Valmont steals 20/25/30/35/40% Attack Speed from the target, and the Target is both Slowed by 25% and are Grounded.

While the Tether is attached, if the Target moves 1800u away from Valmont, breaks Line of Sight from him, or if Valmont is hit by an Immobilizing Effect, the Tether breaks.

Exsanguinate \:

CD: 25/15/5s

Cost: 15 Mana per Second (+5 Mana for each second Exsanguinate remains active).

Effect: Valmont spreads his wings and transforms into an enhanced form. While in this form, Valmont automatically fires out up to 3 swarms of bats each second to nearby Enemy Units within a 1200u radius, dealing 40/70/100 (+22% Magical Power) Magical Damage. After striking, the bats return to Valmont, Healing him for 25/45/65 (+20% Magical Power) Health.

Exsanguinate’s Healing has 10% effectiveness against Non-Heroes.

Augments:

Vein Splitter:

Relevant Ability: Arterial Grip \

Type: Area of Effect

Effect: Arterial Grip’s Blood Tether no longer Grounds targets, but automatically branches to nearby Enemy Targets within 800u of the Primary Target, dealing 80% the damage and applying 100% of the Slow.

Rupturing Fangs:

Relevant Ability: Rupture \

Type: Finisher

Effect: Blades deal 20% less damage, but their damage increases by up to 100% based on the Target's Missing Health.

Sanguine Banquet:

Relevant Ability: Hemophagia \
:

Type: Scaling

Effect: Gain 2% (+0.5% Bonus Mana) Omnivamp. Additionally, Minion Deaths near the Lilith permanently increase Valmont's Maximum Mana by 2, increasing to 30 for Hero Deaths.

Crucible 3v3 Mode

Crucible is a brand new, 3v3 game mode where two teams battle it out on a single lane map with a Jungle area. This is one of the most highly requested game modes we’ve ever had, so we’re super excited for you to get stuck in and see what you think!

Crucible Mechanics Breakdown:

Win condition:

- The Game ends when either team's Core is destroyed.

Removed Buffs:

- Gold Buff has been removed from this mode.
- Cyan Buff has been removed from this mode.
- Orb Prime has been removed but its Buff Effect has been added to Shaper when it is killed.
- Fangtooth has been replaced with a pack of 3 Raptor Fangteeth.

Fangtooth:

- Has been replaced with 3 Raptor Fangteeth.
- A pack of 3 Raptors spawn every 3 minutes.
- Each Raptor slain will grant that team a stack of Trouble. Each stack of Trouble grants a permanent +2% stat increase for all stats, for all Allies on the killing team (No stack limit).
- Health: 3000 (+1500 per level).
- Physical Armor 30 (+8 per level).
- Magical Armor 25 (+1 per level).

Shaper:

- In addition to him spawning a seedling down the lane of the enemy team when killed, the Shaper also granted the but shaper now grants Orb Prime Buff.
- Spawn Time: 10:00.
- Health: 4800 (+1000 per level).
- Physical Armor: 90.
- Magical Armor: 75.

Jungle Monsters/Buffs

Red Stats:

- Health: 2550 (+110 per level).
- Physical Armor: 8.
- Magical Armor: -15 (-1 per level).
- Buff Dropping from game start.
- Only 1 Red Buff in the center of the map.

Blue Stats:

- Health: 950 (+200 per level).
- Physical Armor: 8.
- Magical Armor -15 (-1 per level).
- Buff Dropping from game start.
- 2 Blue Buffs, one in each jungle.

5 Camp Stats:

Medium:

- Health 600 +50 per level
- Armor 5
- Magical Armor 20

Additional Crucible Mechanics:

Geysers:

- Full air control geysers have been added to the map to allow very quick and explosive controlled rotations/playmaking

Gold Plants:

- Spawn at 40s.
- Respawn every 80s.

Speed Plants:

- Spawn at 5s.
- Respawn every 80s.

Bounce Pads:

- Various Bounce Pads are present Spawn in the center of the map to allow fast vertical rotations towards the Shaper Pit. Walk over them to bounce upwards.

Health Packs:

- Health packs are present on the map. Walk over them to trigger a short channel, after which all Heroes that remain in the Zone are healed.

Stealth Bushes:

- Various Bushes are present on the map. Enter them to become stealthed and hidden from Enemies, unless they are also in the Bush, or they have a Ward inside of it.

Player:

- Starting Level: 1
- Starting Gold: 350
- +3 Mana Regen per second
- Gold per Second: 9.5/9.5/9.5/9.5/9.5/11/11/11/12/12/13/13/13/13/13/15/15/15/15/15 (Scale every 60s)
- Blink 150s cooldown
- Jungle XP share 100%

PCC Fall kicks off the 26th of September and is the last chance to secure pinnacle points for your team ahead of the Winter Invitational.

Sign ups close Friday the 18th, head over to the PCC discord before it’s too late. https://t.co/vrJ1RDVtDv

PCC Fall will run over 2 weekends with $8000 up for grabs split across the NA and EU regions. Teams will also receive Pinnacle Points which will be needed to get an invitation to the Winter Invitational. Hey Champions,

It’s time for another Balance Patch! This week, we’ve got a whole bunch of balance tweaks and some incredible new skins!

We’ve seen a lot of discussion over the last couple of weeks about the new Eternals introduced in Update 1.16: Aegis of Dawn. We really appreciate all of your feedback, and our team has made a number of adjustments to bring these new Eternals in line with the originals.

We'll be keeping an eye out for your feedback once this update launches, so please jump on Reddit or Discord to let us know what you think.

Let’s dive in!

Eternal Bundle Core

In Update 1.14 we added a bunch of new Icons and Banners for each Eternal, and made them exclusive drops from Ion cores. We know a lot of players were happy with this, but the main feedback pointed at their rarity and the lack of duplication protection, which made them more of a frustrating experience rather than an exciting one.

The Eternal Bundle Core is a Common Loot Core drop from Ion Cores and has a 4% drop rate, the following rates were changed to support this.

- Common Amber was 12% now 10%
- Common Banner was 11% now 10%
- Common Profile Icons was 11% now 10%

Balance Changes

Head over to the website for the full list of changes!

[p]Hey Champions![/p][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"]It feels like only yesterday we were talking about Ikra, and now we’re here with another update already! We’ve got an awesome new Offlaner, four new Eternals, some incredible new skins, and Brawl Mode is making a comeback! Let’s take a look.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="9-wjL8VUBzw;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h2]New Hero: Scarlett[/h2][p align="start"]In a world where ancient magic intertwines with feudal tradition, a champion of light walks a dark, perilous path. Raised in the ways of combat by her grandmother, Scarlett grew to become a sworn servant of the people, a champion of justice whose kindness is matched only by her mastery of the blade.[/p][p align="start"]For years, her path was clear: defend the helpless and serve as a beacon of hope for those in need. But when a dark, tragic fate struck her beloved, cursing him with a beastly burden, her life was irrevocably altered.[/p][p align="start"]Refusing to let the darkness claim the one she loves, Scarlett now travels the land seeking a cure for his dark curse. Guided by her inquisitive nature and an unyielding knowledge of the wilds, she walks a perilous road between light and shadow. Armed with a blazing spirit, her precise rapier, and a chain lantern to light the way, Scarlett stands ready to illuminate the battlefield and destroy anyone who threatens the innocent.[/p][h3][b]Stats:[/b][/h3][quote][p]- Health: 680 (+136 per Level)
- Health Regen: 1.8 (+0.2 per Level)
- Energy: 200 (+0 per Level)
- Energy Regen: 10 (+0 per Level)
- Attack Speed: 150 (+1.8 per Level)
- Physical Armor: 35 (+5 per Level)
- Magical Armor: 33 (+1.7 per Level)
- Physical Power: 61 (+3.2 per Level)
- Movement Speed: 690
- BAT: 1.55[/p][/quote][h3][b]Abilities:[/b][/h3][p]Last Light \[Passive]:[/p][p align="start"][b]Effect[/b]: Scarlett uses Energy instead of Mana. Additionally, she gains 1 Physical Power for every 40 Bonus Mana she owns.[/p][quote][p]- Max Energy: 200.
- Scarlett restores 10 Energy per Second.
- Takedowns restore 100 Energy.
- Scarlett’s Final Basic Attack in her Chain restores 5 Energy On-Hit, increased to 10 against Enemy Heroes.
- Empowered Cindara restores 35/45/55 Energy (Levels 1/7/13) on Hero or Camp Leader hit.
- First Intent restores 50 Energy for each Unique Hero or Camp Leader hit.
- Swan Song grants +5 Energy Regen while the Ablaze Buff is Active.[/p][/quote][p]Cindara \[Basic Attack]:[/p][p align="start"]Type: Melee[/p][p align="start"]Range: 375u[/p][p align="start"][b]Effect:[/b] Melee Basic attack dealing 61 (+80% Bonus Physical Power) Physical Damage.[/p][quote][p]- Attack Chain: 3 strikes (resets on Ability cast)
- Chain Speed: 2x/2x/1.05x
- Chain Damage: 0.5x/0.5x/1.1x
- Chain On-Hit Modifier: 0.5x/0.5x/1.1x
- Third Strike: Restores 5 Energy On-Hit (increased to 10 against Heroes).
- Empowered: Scarlett equips her lantern for 1 attack, slamming it forward in a 700u line that damages all Enemies hit.[/p][/quote][p]Ashen Vow \[Primary]:[/p][p align="start"][b]CD:[/b] 9/8.25/7.5/6.75/6[/p][p align="start"][b]Cost:[/b] 50 Energy[/p][p align="start"][b]Effect:[/b] Scarlett channels for a short duration, before swinging her lantern in a wide fiery cylinder around her in a 560u radius, dealing 50/75/105/125/150 (+60% Bonus Physical Power) Physical Damage.[/p][p align="start"]Enemies in the outer 255u of the cylinder receive 25/50/75/100/125 (+100% Bonus Physical Power) additional Physical Damage, and are Slowed by 35%/37.5%/40%/42.5%/45% for 1.25s.[/p][p align="start"]If Scarlett hits an Enemy Hero or Camp Leader with the outer edge, her next Basic Attack is Empowered for 4s to deal 10 (+12% Bonus Physical Power)(+2/3/4/5/6% Target’s Max Health) additional Physical Damage to all Enemies in a 700u line in front of her. Scarlett restores 35/45/55 Energy (Levels 1/7/13) if this hits an Enemy Hero or Camp Leader.[/p][p align="start"]Empowered Cindara’s damage is reduced by 50% against Minions, and capped to 150/200/250/300/350 against Monsters.[/p][p align="start"][b]Ablaze:[/b] While Swan Song is Active, Empowered Cindara’s Bonus Damage is increased by 1.5x.[/p][p]First Intent \[Secondary]:[/p][p align="start"][b]CD:[/b] 16/15/14/13/12[/p][p align="start"][b]Cost:[/b] 80 Energy[/p][p align="start"][b]Effect:[/b] Scarlett dashes forward 1000u with a decisive fiery strike that deals 65/85/105/125/145 (+80% Bonus Physical Power) Physical Damage to all Enemies in her path and receives a 20/70/120/170/220 (+40%/45%/50%/55%/60% Total Physical Power) Shield for 3s.[/p][p align="start"]Each time Scarlett hits an Enemy Hero or Camp Leader with First Intent, she refreshes her Shield’s duration and increases its size by 60%, and restores 50 Energy.[/p][p]Minueta \[Alternate]:[/p][p align="start"][b]CD: [/b]7/6.25/5.5/4.75/4[/p][p align="start"][b]Cost:[/b] 105/95/85/75/65 Energy[/p][p align="start"][b]Effect:[/b] Scarlett twirls in her current movement direction, with its speed increasing based on current momentum. Scarlett then stabs forward 3 times (610u range), with each dealing 21/31/41/51/61 (+24%/28.5%/33%/37.5%/42% Total Physical Power) Physical Damage to all Enemies in the area. The final stab deals up to 100% bonus damage based on the Target’s Missing Health.[/p][p align="start"]Stabs benefit from Lifesteal and can Critically Strike at 60% effectiveness.[/p][p align="start"][b]Ablaze:[/b] While Swan Song is active, the number of stabs is increased to 4, dealing +15% more damage overall.[/p][p]Swan Song \[Ultimate]:[/p][p align="start"]Cooldown: 125/105/85[/p][p align="start"]Cost: 0[/p][p align="start"][b]Effect:[/b] Scarlett winds up over 0.6s before thrusting forward (825u) with her Lantern, Restraining (Uncleansable Stun) the first Enemy Hero hit for 1.4s, and Slowing nearby Enemies within a 600u radius by 65% for 1s.[/p][p align="start"]Scarlett then backflips into the air, becoming Unstoppable for the duration of the Restrain, and ignites her blade before striking down at the target, dealing 180/280/380 (+100% Bonus Physical Power) Physical Damage.[/p][p align="start"]Enemies within a 600u radius of the Restrained Target take 100% of the strike’s damage.[/p][p align="start"]Afterwards, Scarlett’s Blade is Ablaze for the next 8/10/12s, granting her +150 Basic Attack Range, +5 Energy Regen, and +20/32/44 (+12% Bonus Physical Power) Physical Power for the duration. Additionally, Empowered Cindara and Minueta are empowered to deal more damage during this time.[/p][h3][b]Augments:[/b][/h3][p]Scarlet Dawn:[/p][p align="start"][b]Related Ability:[/b] First Intent \[Secondary][/p][p align="start"][b]Type:[/b] Mobility[/p][p align="start"][b]Effect:[/b] Ability, Empowered Cindara, and Third Strike hits on Enemy Heroes & Camp Leaders reduce First Intent’s Cooldown by 8%, reduced to 5% for Minueta hits.[/p][p]Coup De Grace:[/p][p align="start"][b]Related Ability:[/b] Swan Song \[Ultimate][/p][p align="start"][b]Type:[/b] Dueling[/p][p align="start"][b]Effect:[/b] Swan Song marks the Restrained target. If they die within 8/10/12s, Ablaze extends by 5s, and a fiery zone appears beneath the dead target for 5s that heals Yourself and Allies by 100/150/200 (+65% Bonus Physical Power) each second.[/p][p]Volcanic Slam:[/p][p align="start"][b]Related Ability:[/b] Ashen Vow \[Primary][/p][p align="start"][b]Type:[/b] Zone Control[/p][p align="start"][b]Effect:[/b] Enhanced Cindara leaves behind a rupture that erupts after 0.5s. The eruption deals 20 (+4 per Level) (+25% Bonus Physical Power) True Damage to all Enemies in the area and Slows them by 40% for 1.25s.[/p][h2]Store News[/h2][h3][b]Celestial Gideon \[Epic][/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34481624/7405567aa69513780228636be3a69a940c26ddde.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Celestial Sevarog \[Epic][/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34481624/09553dd8ca61ff11d05d3bd07a4953af1d1328ca.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]Galaxy Zinx \[Epic][/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34481624/6316055fb07593c3b7033cf255bab79023319ef8.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Celestial Serath \[Rare][/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34481624/dfbfa546f5cc5631e70e1a2f5abe8fc44f73096b.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Origin Scarlett \[Rare][/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34481624/9017a22481996ff56978f69845380af87f1be860.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]Origin Scarlett Bundle[/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34481624/c1896ad7cdee69b2d8a0a30dd28098a6e3fb5bf0.png"][/img][/p][quote][p]- Origin Scarlett \[Skin]

Be the first team to get the Enemy’s Ticket Score to zero to win![/p][p align="start"]For its return, not only has the Brawl map received some changes to its layout and visuals, but various mechanics have also been switched up that aim to make the mode more fun and resolve some of the pain points raised from its previous iteration.[/p][p align="start"]The full details can be found below in the Brawl Mechanics Breakdown section, but the major points to note are:[/p][quote][p]- Win Condition: When a Team reaches 50 Tickets, Minion Deaths no longer reduce the Score. However, we will enable multi-hero selection for special dates and events, so keep an eye on our socials![/p][/quote][p align="start"][i]Known Issue: Replays do not currently work for Brawl Mode.[/i][/p][h3][b]Brawl Mechanics Breakdown[/b][/h3][p]Win condition[/p][quote][p]- The game ends when a team's tickets reach Zero.

Picking up the Buff Orb will grant the player the following buff based on the color.[/p][p]Giant Stats:[/p][quote][p]- Health 2000 (+500 per Level).

- Damage 40 (+8 per Level) .[/p][/quote][p]Orange Buff:[/p][quote][p]- Duration: 45s
- Effects: Become Unstoppable and gain +6% Max Health Regen per second.[/p][/quote][p]Blue Buff:[/p][quote][p]- Duration: 45s

Hey Champions!

It feels like only yesterday we were talking about Ikra, and now we’re here with another update already! We’ve got an awesome new Offlaner, four new Eternals, some incredible new skins, and Brawl Mode is making a comeback! Let’s take a look.

New Hero: Scarlett

In a world where ancient magic intertwines with feudal tradition, a champion of light walks a dark, perilous path. Raised in the ways of combat by her grandmother, Scarlett grew to become a sworn servant of the people, a champion of justice whose kindness is matched only by her mastery of the blade.

For years, her path was clear: defend the helpless and serve as a beacon of hope for those in need. But when a dark, tragic fate struck her beloved, cursing him with a beastly burden, her life was irrevocably altered.

Refusing to let the darkness claim the one she loves, Scarlett now travels the land seeking a cure for his dark curse. Guided by her inquisitive nature and an unyielding knowledge of the wilds, she walks a perilous road between light and shadow. Armed with a blazing spirit, her precise rapier, and a chain lantern to light the way, Scarlett stands ready to illuminate the battlefield and destroy anyone who threatens the innocent.

Brawl Mode

Brawl returns! Shiny, new, and very much improved thanks to your feedback! We’ve made some changes to the ruleset, buffs and the map itself.

For those of you that are new to Brawl, it is a fast-paced, 5v5 gamemode where each team has a ticket score that gets reduced each time a Hero dies, Minions die, or when Minions are pushed into the enemy team’s portal. Be the first team to get the Enemy’s Ticket Score to zero to win!

For its return, not only has the Brawl map received some changes to its layout and visuals, but various mechanics have also been switched up that aim to make the mode more fun and resolve some of the pain points raised from its previous iteration.

The full details can be found below in the Brawl Mechanics Breakdown section, but the major points to note are:

- Win Condition: When a Team reaches 50 Tickets, Minion Deaths no longer reduce the Score. Only Hero Kills and Minions entering a Portal can reduce Tickets below 50.
- Orb Prime: Orb Prime no longer spawns in the middle of the map at 10-minutes.
- Lane Fangteeth: No longer appear each time a team has 5 Hero Deaths.
- Giant and Jump Height Buff: The Brown and Pink Golems have been removed and replaced by Cyan Buffs, with New Buffs now being present in the middle of the Map!
- New Buffs: Instead of Orb Prime and Lane Fangtooth, there are now 2 Buffs that appear on either side of the map, spawning every 2-minutes. The Buffs are a range of new Giant Golems that provide powerful effects to the killer's team by collecting a Buff Orb, such as super speed, increased size, Double-Ultimate, and more!
- Primal Fangtooth: Will now also appear at one of these New Buff Spawn Locations, every 2nd spawn. The Team that kills the Primal Fangtooth will now have it spawn on their side of the map, with it charging down the Lane towards the Enemies Portal, scoring a large amount of Tickets if it makes it into the Enemies Portal!
- Multiple Heroes On The Same Team: Heroes are once again limited to 1-per team, meaning you can no longer play 5 of the same Hero on the same team. However, we will enable multi-hero selection for special dates and events, so keep an eye on our socials!

Known Issue: Replays do not currently work for Brawl Mode.

Brawl Mechanics Breakdown

Win condition

- The game ends when a team's tickets reach Zero.
- When a team has only 50 tickets remaining, minion kills no longer reduce tickets.
- Only Hero kills and Portal kills reduce tickets at sub 50 Tickets.

Quality Of Life Improvements

New Critical Health SFX Cue:

Practice Mode has had the following adjustments and additions:

- Haste Capsule now refreshes all Cooldowns when activated.
- There is a new Capsule to Evolve your Crest a stage per hit.
- There is a new Capsule to fully stack stacking Items and/or add some stacks to infinite stacking Items.

Camp Despawning:

- Once the Camp Leader of a Normal Jungle Camp is killed (2/3/4/5 Camp), the remaining Monsters will now despawn after 10s of not being in combat.

Fountain Diving:

- Enemy Fountains no longer 1-shot you upon entering their Zone.
- Upon standing in the Enemy Fountain’s Zone, you now receive ramping true damage instead.
- There is a new Camera Lens Effect & SFX to signify when you enter the Enemy Team’s Fountain.

Client Prediction Adjustments & Blink Rubberbanding:

- Certain abilities (such as Boris Ultimate, Ranged Basic Attacks, Melee Basic Attacks, Bayle Ultimate, and Crunch Empowered Right Crunch will no longer yoink you back or hit you if you manage to get a small distance away from the original location, such as by blinking out of their path.

Enhanced Airborne Hero Shadows:

- Ally and Enemy Heroes now cast a shadowy decal beneath their location on the ground when they are in the air.
- This will make it easier to tell where Flying Heroes such as Howitzer and Wukong precisely are when they are above you, as you will be able to see their shadow directly below them on the ground.

Respawned Inhibitor Clarity:

- Respawned Inhibitors now show a purple material around them to signify they are disabled and do not attack, adding more clarity.

Buff Dropping (Red/Blue/Mini):

Mini Prime:

- Mini Prime now drops its buff on the floor slightly in front of it when it dies, rather than being granted to the killer. The Buffs last for 30s on the floor.
- The first Ally Hero to walk over it gets it. Enemy Heroes cannot pick it up but it will appear greyscale for them at the location.

Red & Blue Buff:

- From 20:00 onwards, Red & Blue Buff now drop an ADDITIONAL Buff Pickup at their original spawn location, that lasts in the world for 30s.
- The first Ally Hero to walk over it gets it. Enemy Heroes cannot pick it up but it will appear greyscale for them at the location.
- Red & Blue Buff are now a slightly different Color when Buff Dropping is active (at 20:00).
- In other words, Junglers can now kill their Buffs late-game, and let an Ally pick up an additional copy of that buff.

Tower Platings Expanded:

- Tier 1 Outer Tower Platings no longer disappear at 13 minutes and are now present for the entire match.
- Tier 2 Inner Towers now also have Tower Platings for the entire match.

Ground Targeting Improvements:

- Ground targeting abilities now aim directly from the Camera reticle, rather than from the Hero’s model. This will reduce the amount of times an ability clips against a wall unintentionally.
- Ground targeting abilities now place at the centre of your reticle, rather than being slightly offset to the left.

Aim Assist Tuning:

- Aim Assist for Controllers has been adjusted to be slightly less sticky, while improving other areas of it that should make the gameplay experience smoother for Controller Users.

Item Effect Stat Tracking:

- A variety of Items now track various stats (such as how much damage they have dealt in a game, among other stats). To see them, hover over yours (or another Player’s) Items on the scoreboard.

Recalls - Damage Over Time (DoT):

- Damage Over Time (DoT) Damage Effects no longer interrupt Recalls.

Hey Champions,

It’s balance time! Eternals totally shook up the meta since their arrival in 1.14, it’s been awesome to see how you’ve all been building and adapting with them.

This update is a larger balance pass to correct some issues we’ve seen with Eternals. We’re expecting a little more will be needed until we find that sweet spot though, so keep your feedback coming in!

Store News

Iron Guard Riktor \

Deadzone Drongo \

Bundles

The Victorious skins are back for a limited time, with some new additions, to support the PCC Summer Summit. All profits from the skin sales go towards supporting competitive Predecessor events!

Victorious Summer Bundle

Bundle Cores

We are introducing a new type of loot core in this patch called Bundle Cores. These cores will be available for limited time and contain a small collection of content, with no duplicate drops and every drop shares the same drop rate.

Premium Bundle Core - Contains 2 exclusive variants for Iron Guard Riktor and Deadzone Drongo plus a selection of previously available bundle exclusive variants from last year.

Victorious Bundle Core - Contains all victorious skins and a new Recall and Jumppad exclusive to this Bundle Core. Profits from this Core go directly to supporting Predecessor Competitive Events.

ARAM Battlepass XP changes

Players shared feedback that with the introduction of quests too much XP was removed from ARAM as a lot of the quests are harder to complete when playing ARAM. We agreed so we are increasing the amount of Battlepass XP gained from playing ARAM by 60%.

Thank you to everyone that shared feedback on the topic.

PCC Summer Summit

The PCC Summer Summit is here and will be kicking off with a 3-weekend event, starting on the 13th and 14th of June at 10 AM EDT/ 2PM UTC on the Predecessor Twitch channel. We'll also be co-streaming with some of your favourite content creators too!

Teams in EU and NA will be competing for a total prize pool of $14,000 and representation in Predecessor via 2d Cosmetics.

More info on the event here.

We will be running Twitch drops during the event weekends, as well as Platinum giveaways, so tune in to pick up some new content!

New OHE available from Twitch drops.

Victorious Cosmetics

The prize pool and event costs for tournaments like this and other community events come from the profits made from the Victorious content. If you would like to support future events please consider picking up any of the Victorious skins, bundles and more!

New Victorious Skins coming in 1.14.4

We have introduced a Victorious Bundle Core to further support competitive events, which contains all Victorious Skins and a new Victorious Recall and Jumppad exclusive to the Bundle Core. Bundle Cores do not drop duplicate items.

Lastly it’s been requested for there to be more ways to donate towards Esports, so we are introducing a Luxury Donation Cosmetic. This Epic OHE is intended for those wishing to make a larger donation to PCC, so only consider purchasing this if you are willing to make that type of donation. 100% of the sales from this OHE will go into supporting Competitive events.

Balance Changes

Overview:

For this pass, we are primarily looking at smoothing out the gameplay experience and tidying up some of the balance/gameplay loop fallout that has occurred with the addition of the Eternals and the power they have provided. Specifically, this is being done by rounding out the rough edges for some of the more extreme balance outliers and Eternals that are causing extreme power spikes or offering too much/too little general value, with it hopefully resulting in a more well-rounded balance baseline. As we mentioned in the v1.14 update, our plan moving forward is to continue refining the balance ecosystem with the new Eternals in mind, which naturally will take a few more passes to get into a nice and stable spot, but for now this should be a positive step forward.

- Addition of some new Magical Power and Physical Power hybrid scalings to various Hero Abilities, opening up Eternal and Build diversity further.
- Tower Durability & Damage increased.
- Minion Durability increased.
- Hunt’s Slay Damage increased to 600/1200.
- Monster Durability increased slightly to compensate for the Hunt change.
- Various adjustments and reworks to Eternal Blessings to help address problem-cases, or make the lesser-picked options more viable in strength compared to the more popular options.
- Small increases to the base damage of various abilities (primarily Mages and Bruisers) to ensure their damage stays a little more relevant at the Level 3-9 thresholds as Durability spikes can result in the inability to adequately threaten kills at that range.
- General Hero Balance to bring the extreme outliers further into general parity.
- Buffs to some Fighter and Anti-tank Items.
- ARAM Tower Durability/Damage increases.
- And more!

Check out all the balance changes on our website!

Hey Champions!

V1.14: Harbingers of Ruin is almost upon us, an update which is sure to redefine the meta with Eternals, our biggest Hero customisation system ever, as well as an incredible new Hero and more! Let’s dive in.

New Hero: Legion

From the world of Aresium comes the highly decorated shock trooper, Legion. A fanatical hand of an empire dedicated to bringing the galaxy under a single, united rule. Produced for absolute loyalty and peak efficiency, he has survived countless battles as a disciplined instrument of the Aresium Empire, a force that seeks to "liberate" the stars from the chaos of tyrannical freedom.

For generations, his batch-engineered brothers have served as a righteous hand of order, mastering the arts of battlefield logistics and ballistic weaponry to crush any who would oppose their mandate. As a total believer in the cause, Legion revels in the destruction of his enemies, finding his greatest joy in fighting and dying for the glorious empire that gave him life.

Legion’s newest mission has seen him deployed as a heavy-weapons anchor to far-flung battlefields, tasked with enforcing imperial doctrine by any means necessary. He descends upon the front line not as a mere soldier, but as a siege engine of order, stopping at nothing to ensure total purification and the expansion of the Empire’s reach.

Stats

- Health: 660 (+132 per Level)
- Health Regen: 1.4 (+0.15 per Level)
- Mana: 350 (+46 per level)
- Mana Regen: 1.5 (+0.18 per level)
- Attack Speed: 100 (+0 per Level)
- Physical Armor: 30 (+5.1 per Level)
- Magical Armor: 29 (+1.15 per Level)
- Physical Power: 20 (+2 per Level)
- Movement Speed: 665
- BAT: 0.2

Abilities

Ballistic Calibration \
:

Effect: Trooper converts 1% Bonus Attack Speed into 0.75 Ability Haste. He also gains bonuses based on the Stat Thresholds he reaches:

- 100 Physical Power: Saturation Charge Slow Duration increased by 0.75s.
- 30 Physical Penetration: Orbital Sanction Radius increased by 33%.
- 50 Ability Haste: Frag Order deals additional damage equal to 10% of the Target’s Missing Health.
- 100 Magical Power: Rally Point Health Regeneration is increased by 50%.

K-75 Storm Rifle \:

Type: Ranged

Range: 1500u

Effect: Legion’s K-75 Storm Rifle fires at a fixed rate of 1 Round every 0.2s, with a 15 Round Mag.

Legion’s Rifle Regenerates Ammo at a rate of 1 per 0.2s after not attacking for 1.25s, and he will automatically Reload if his Mag’ is fully exhausted.

Each shot deals 20 (+17% Bonus Physical Power) Physical Damage, increased by 1.25% per 1 Physical Penetration Legion possesses.

Saturation Charge \
:

CD: 20/19/18/17/16s

Cost: 70/75/80/85/90 Mana

Effect: Legion fires a heavy payload that deploys 10 Cluster Mines upon hitting the world or upon reactivation. Each Cluster Mine deals 35/45/55/65/75 (+50% Bonus Physical Power)(+40% Magical Power) Physical Damage and Slows targets hit by 40% for 1s.

Cluster Mine damage is decreased to 25% against the same Target for subsequent Mine hits beyond the first.

Rally Point \:

CD: 30/28.5/27/25.5/24s

Cost: 35 Mana

Effect: Legion becomes Unstoppable for 0.5s and slams his Standard into the ground at his feet, dealing 20/25/30/35/40 (+20% Bonus Physical Power) Physical Damage and Knocking Back nearby enemies.

The Standard creates a large zone that lasts for 8s. While in the zone, Legion gains Infinite Ammo. Legion and Allied Heroes also gain 8% Movement Speed and 5/8/11/14/17 (+110% Physical Penetration)(+10% Magical Power) Health Regeneration while in the zone.

The Standard also provides Vision and reveals Enemy Wards in its local area.

Frag Order \:

CD: 16/15/14/13/12s

Cost: 50

Effect: Legion prepares a grenade with a 2.2s fuse, able to hold it to cook the grenade, reducing the time before its detonation.

Upon releasing, Legion lobs the grenade to a target location, dealing 70/110/150/190/230 (+60/65/70/75/80% Bonus Physical Power)(+40% Magical Power) Physical Damage upon detonation.

The grenade will automatically explode after 0.2s if it detects an Enemy Unit within a 300u radius.

If Legion is caught in the explosion, he will be displaced upwards. If Legion holds the grenade for the full 2.2s, it explodes in his hand. If Legion is Stunned or Killed while cooking the grenade, it will drop to the floor.

Orbital Sanction \:

CD: 140/125/110s

Cost: 100

Effect: Legion lobs a target designator that deploys upon landing. After a 0.75s delay, a beam of energy emanating from the atmosphere will blast the location and follow the nearest target (prioritising Heroes) for 6/7.5/9s. If no targets are within 2000 units of the Beam, it will remain stationary.

Enemy Units caught in the beam take 30/50/70 (+28% Bonus Physical Power)(+10% Magical Power) Physical Damage every 0.25s.

Augments

Heavy Caliber:

Relevant Ability: K-75 Storm Rifle \

Type: Basic Attacks

Effect: Legion’s rate of fire is decreased to 0.75s and his Mag’ Size is reduced from 15 to 6. However, his shots deal 440% damage and have +100 Range.

Scorched Earth:

Relevant Ability: General

Type: Zone Control

Effect: Frag Order and Saturation Charge’s Mine create 300u radius Napalm zones upon exploding, and Orbital Sanction creates one at its location every 0.5s. Napalm zones last for 3s and deal 5 (+6% Bonus Physical Power) Physical Damage every 0.5s to Enemies in the area.

Press The Advantage:

Relevant Ability: Rally Point \

Type: Attack Speed

Effect: Upon achieving a Takedown, a Standard is spawned at the dead target's location. Rally Point no longer grants Health Regeneration, but increases Legion’s Fire Rate by 10/12.5/15/17.5/20% and grants Allies 10/12.5/15/17.5/20% Attack Speed.

Ion Cores

We’re also adding a bunch of Eternals Icons and Banners into Ion Cores as temporarily exclusive drops! These cosmetics will be available in the store at a later date and will be available for purchase with Amber.

Battlepass

The Harbingers of Ruin battlepass is here! Filled to the brim with awesome rewards on both the free and paid tracks.

Eternals

Eternals are powerful deities in the Predecessor universe, capable of granting meta-defining “blessings” to worthy Heroes who choose to follow them.

This is a massive new gameplay system that redefines Hero customisation in the game, enabling you to pick from a huge range of Blessings for any Hero you want. Blessings range from high-risk berserker types, who thrive under near-death situations with extreme lifesteal, to unbreakable tanks who scale Max HP infinitely, and everything in between!

How Eternals Works

Eternals are a new gameplay customization feature, replacing the Minor Augments. Eternals allow Players to select one of twelve Deities during the Draft Phase of a Match, based on their gameplay preferences.

Each Deity offers the Player that selects them a powerful unique Major Blessing which is a Passive Effect that persists throughout a match.

Additionally, after choosing an Eternal, Players can choose 2 additional Minor Blessings from 2 sets of 3 Minor Blessings that are unique to that specific Eternal.

Eternal Blessings, like Augments, are active from Match start and, once selected for the first time, will be remembered across matches on a per Hero, per role basis, unless you change them. This means if you pick Eternals for Argus in Midlane, and want to play him again in your next match in the same role, the system will remember. If you take him into Support instead, it will go back to the recommended until you change your Eternals for Argus in Support.

In simpler terms, you now start the match with:

- 1 Hero Augment.
- 1 Eternal Major Blessing.
- 2 Eternal Minor Blessings.

Unlocking Eternals

All 12 Eternals will be unlocked when a player reaches level 10. Players that have not yet reached Level 10 will automatically be given pre-determined Eternals, and respective Minor Blessings, based on their Hero/Role chosen.

Types of Eternals

Eternals are thematically grouped based on gameplay archetypes and lore. However, these groupings are not prescriptive for gameplay, so we encourage Players to experiment with the Eternals.

In other words, this means that you do not necessarily need to take a “Carry Eternal” while playing as a Carry in order to find success, and could try a “Fighter” or “Supportive” Eternal instead if they synergize well with your Hero or Build!

Find out more about Eternals here

Daybreak V5

We’ve got another substantial update coming to Daybreak, our new WIP map! We’ve been hard at work going through your feedback from the last version to bring a bunch of highly requested additions and changes to improve the flow and overall gameplay experience.

V5 should improve the following core pain points:

- Jungle flow should feel better in terms of Navigation and Pathing
- Junglers attempting to gank lanes from a Camp should find the flow a lot more natural.
- The constant pressure and chaos of the River Bugs in the Jungle respawning repeatedly should be reduced and the Jungle Bugs should make Jungle pathing feel more intentional and tactical.
- Moments where a Player hits dead-ends due to unintuitive terrain and feeling trapped as a result should be reduced significantly.
- Shrines grant side-lanes an additional mini-objective to fight over for increased interaction, reducing the frequency of freeze-heavy/overly passive gameplay.
- The map feeling overly large should feel reduced through the combination of layout and aesthetic changes applied.
- Game Speed should feel slightly faster and more engaging, with the additional gold and XP available on the map (and the adjustments to the objectives helping to provide new areas to contest) helping games to wrap up more naturally between the 25-35m mark.
- Various Bugfixes regarding the Terrain and Collisions.

Overall, by taking our learnings from the feedback offered on v3/v4, and actioning the largest pain points expressed by Players in previous tests, with Daybreak v5 we have hopefully created something that Players enjoy a lot more, both in terms of moment-to-moment gameplay and how it feels to explore and navigate. So be sure to let us know what you think on Discord and Reddit!

Daybreak V5 - Mechanics Breakdown

Terrain & Layout Changes

- General adjustments to the elevation/height around the map to feel less steep.
- Full Rework of both Jungles, including their Terrain and Camp locations.
- Lane entrances Reworked for all 3 lanes, further improving the approaches and Line Of Sight (LOS) issues in previous versions.
- Increased the size of the Bases for both Teams, primarily around the Core area.
- Fangtooth and Orb Prime Pits general Layout and Size Adjustments.
- Midlane reworked with various adjustments to its curvature and landscape.
- Duolane slight rework, primarily targeting improvements around the previously unhealthy Bush locations and the overly punishing gameplay they promoted.
- Offlane slight rework, primarily to make the lane feel a little more interactive and dynamic on the edges of the lane, and less of an Island that made others feel unable to interact with it.
- Distance between Towers and general spacing adjusted.

Objectives

Shrines

- Added New Objective: Shrines
- Locations:
- Inner side of Duolane.
- Inner Side of Offlane.
- Initial Spawn Time: 120s.
- Respawn Time: Every 120s.
- Shrine Rewards:
- Grants 25 Gold.
- Grants 50 Global Gold.
- Permanently grants the Killer +2 Ability Haste.
- Grants a Team-wide Buff on Kill:
- Shrine Buff:
- Global Team Buff granting +8% Damage against Towers.
- The Buff is twice as effective if both Shrines are controlled by the same team.
- Buff Duration: 120s.
- Shrine States:
- Grey: Ready to Kill
- Blue: Your Team has killed the Shrine and is gaining the Buff.
- Red: The Enemy Team has killed the Shrine and is gaining the Buff.
- Shrine Stats:
- Health: 900.
- Health Regen: 0.

Jungle River Bugs

- Jungle River Buffs Replaced with Jungle Bugs:
- They are always the same type of River Bug and called “Jungle Bugs” to differentiate them:
- Red Jungle = Orange Bug.
- Blue Jungle = Pink Bug.
- Note: For testing simplicity, they currently have the same stats and grant the same Buffs as their River counterparts, but do not Evolve.
- Initial Spawn Time: 210s.
- Respawn Time: 120s (No longer on a fixed 2m spawn cycle like River Bugs).

Gold & Cyan Buff Balance

- Gold Buff now grants more Gold, but less XP.
- Cyan Buff now grants more XP, but less Gold.

Plus lots more! Head over to our website to see the full list of changes!
